title: Canoe Camping in Killarney 2
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-2)**

**Dive into the Killarney backcountry with this beautiful and beginner friendly canoe camping adventure.**

We're heading to Bell Lake, on the quieter east side of the park, for a weekend that mixes an easy paddle-in camping trip and an incredible hike to Silver Peak, the highest point in Killarney.

Friday, we'll paddle the short 2.5km crossing to our backcountry site, set up camp, and spend the afternoon settling in. The rest of the afternoon is yours to spend how you like. If you want to learn to pitch a tent, get a fire going properly, or handle a canoe, we'll show you. If you'd rather find a rock in the sun and do nothing, that works too.

Saturday, you can chill around camp or paddle over and hike Silver Peak, the highest point in the park. It's a roughly 11km round trip, starting on an easy rolling trail before a steep, hands on scramble up exposed quartzite for the final push. At the top, you're rewarded with a 360 degree view over Killarney's white ridges and out to Georgian Bay. Trust us, you won’t get many views in Ontario that are better than this!

Both nights, we'll eat around the fire and fall asleep under some of the clearest skies in Ontario. Killarney's stargazing is genuinely other-worldly. On a clear night you'll see the Milky Way and more stars than you knew existed. Sunday, we pack up and paddle back out.

By Sunday, you'll have spent two days swimming, paddling, and sleeping under the stars, surrounded by Killarney's unmistakable landscapes.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents
* Canoe rentals

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Highlights**
**Silver Peak Summit:** The highest point in Killarney, with sweeping views over the range and out to Georgian Bay
**Stargazing:** With some of the darkest skies in Ontario, the Milky Way is in full view on a clear night
**Lake Swimming:** Cool off in clear water, or take the canoe out for a closer look at the shoreline

**Event cost: $455+HST (for explorer members) - $70 optional transport available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/killarney-camping-2)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

**The Friday Night Mix, Mingle, Dinner and Live Music Party!**

Start your weekend with a fun Friday night of great conversation, new connections, dinner, drinks and live music at Smoke Show!

This is a relaxed social night designed for people who enjoy meeting others without the pressure of a formal singles event.
Come on your own or bring a friend — we’ll have a friendly group ready to mix, mingle and enjoy the evening together.

🍽️ DINNER, DRINKS & CONVERSATION
We’ll start the evening by getting comfortable, ordering some food and drinks, and getting to know one another. Don’t worry if you’re coming alone — many people do! We’ll help introduce people and get the conversations flowing.
🎵 LIVE MUSIC
As the evening gets going, we’ll enjoy live music while continuing to mix and mingle. You can sit back and listen, chat with new friends, grab another drink, or move around and meet more people.
🤝 MEET NEW PEOPLE
The idea is simple: get out of the house, put the phones away for a while and enjoy some real face-to-face socializing. You never know who you might meet — a new friend, someone to join you at future events, or perhaps someone special.

No pressure. No complicated agenda. Just a fun Friday night with good food, good music, good conversation and good company.

You’ll then hear two short sets by small ensembles of expert musicians from a range of musical backgrounds, each exploring spontaneous and unscripted ways of making music together. Expect an evening of surprising sounds, creative energy, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

title: Frontenac Fall Colours Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-colours-frontenac)**

**A true member favourite returns! While the crowds flock to Algonquin to view fall colours, Frontenac is where it's really at.**

By late September, the first maples along this loop are already turning red and gold against bare granite, weeks ahead of peak colour further south. That granite is part of the Frontenac Arch, a two-billion-year-old ridge connecting the Canadian Shield to the Adirondacks, and it's what gives this loop its particular look in fall.

The Cedar Lake South Loop runs about 9km through a mix of open granite, rooted forest trails, and genuine wetland: expect boggy sections, small ponds, and stretches where the water clearly has the upper hand on the trail.

Frontenac sits at an ecological crossover point, where northern species like spruce and balsam fir grow next to southern hardwoods like sugar maple, red oak, and yellow birch. That mix means a wider range of fall colour than you'd get from a single-species forest: deep red, burnt orange, and gold, all held together by the seasonal consistency of the dark green conifers.

By the time we're back at the vehicles, you'll have spent the day walking through some of the best fall colours eastern Ontario has to offer!

**Self drivers please note** \- Frontenac is at least a 3hr drive and requires a $15 day pass \- you're strongly recommended to choose the transport option for this trip\. The day pass is included for anyone riding in the van\.
‍
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to [info@wildernessunion.com](mailto:info@wildernessunion.com)

**Highlights**
**Stunning Fall Colours:** Red and gold hardwoods press right up against bare granite, the loop's sharpest colour contrast.
**Doe Lake Lookout:** A gap in the trees opens onto the full length of Doe Lake, framed by granite shoreline and turning hardwoods.
**Away from the Crowds:** Lesser known spot to enjoy the Fall colours.

**Event cost: $75+HST (for explorer members). Optional transportation available.**
**Register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-colours-frontenac)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: L'univers sombre et magnifique
location: North York Central Library, Room 1, 2e étage (2nd floor)
description:
Depuis des millénaires, les êtres humains contemplent le ciel nocturne et s'interrogent sur l'origine de l'univers. D'où vient-il ? De quoi est-ce fait? Où va-t-il? Dans cette présentation,
Renée Hložek
vous parlerai de cet univers — à la fois sombre et magnifique — et de la manière dont nous utilisons les télescopes pour en percer les secrets.
Renée Hložek
est cosmologiste sud-africaine et professeure agrégée au Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics de l’Université de Toronto. Ses recherches portent sur les origines et l’évolution de l’Univers, notamment le fond diffus cosmologique, l’énergie noire et la matière noire. Elle participe à d’importantes collaborations internationales, telles que l’Atacama Cosmology Telescope, le Simons Observatory et le Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Elle a reçu la médaille du roi Charles III pour la communication d’idées scientifiques, ainsi que la médaille Rutherford et la bourse Arthur B. McDonald du Conseil de recherches en sciences naturelles et en génie du Canada.

**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Welcome to Toronto History Walks!

This walk is the full history and story behind the building of the Leslie Street Spit. From a popular beach in the 1950s to a nature sanctuary this walk explores the human and natural history of the Park!

One of the best places to walk and enjoy the sights of Toronto is Tommy Thompson Park. But it's not just a great place to see the sweeping views of Toronto harbour, but it's also a fascinating story of landfill operations and has an historic undertone that dates back to the early twentieth century.

Out of nothing comes something, really should be the slogan for the Leslie Street Spit.

This walk is not only a history walk, it has some of the best opportunities for picture taking, and nature. So I hope to see you there, and bring your camera.

Our walk begins at the southeast intersection of **Leslie St at Commissioners Street!** We return to the start location after our adventure!

title: Pressed Flowers Necklace Workshop
location: Forest Hill, Program Room
description:
Capture summer’s beauty forever in this hands-on Flower Pressed Necklace Workshop, hosted by Gabriela Delworth. Whether you're a jewelry enthusiast or a nature lover, this session offers a creative space to design a wearable piece of art that lasts forever.
What You Will Discover:
The Art of Pressing: Learn the essential techniques for preserving blooms, including the best time of day to harvest and which flower varieties hold their color and shape best.
Storage Secrets: Master the professional methods for storing pressed flowers to prevent fading and moisture damage.
Jewelry Design: Arrange your choice of delicate petals and greenery into a custom pendant. You will leave with a one-of-a-kind necklace that respects your personal style.
Workshop Details:
All inclusive: Your free registration covers all materials; all participants receive a curated kit by the instructor. Tools are provided by the instructor and returned at the end of the workshop.
Skill Level: Perfect for beginners; no prior experience in jewelry making or gardening is required.

description:
For Children ages 4 to 12 with their parent or caregiver.
This interactive puppet show from Chad Solomon features characters from the Rabbit and Bear Paws children's graphic novel series. In this performance, audiences will experience the story of how the turtle carried our world on her back, and how the tiny muskrat succeeded in giving us the greatest gift of all - a place to call home, Turtle Island.
Chad Solomon
is a member of the Henvey Inlet, First Nation. His grandfather taught him that no matter how old you become, you should always be young-at-heart and that laughter is the greatest medicine. This is the spirit behind the comical Adventures of Rabbit and Bear Paws series.
Drop-in only. No Registration Required.

title: Learn to Spin Your Own Yarn- September
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a three session Beginner Spinning Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday September 26, October 3, and October 10 from 3:00pm-4:30pm Learn how to transform fibre into yarn with our drop spindle class! In this class you will learn how to use a drop spindle to spin starting with woolly fibre and ending with a completed, ready to use yarn. You will learn how to spin a single ply yarn, how to spin a 2-ply yarn using the Andean Plying method, and how to chain ply for a 3-ply yarn over three classes. We will discuss spinning basics as well as different types of yarn, fibres, processing tools, and preparations and how these affect the finished yarn. Drop spindles must be brought by students or purchased in store. 50g of fibre provided in two different colours. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Classes cancelled less than 48 hrs prior to the start of the class will not be reimbursed.

title: 🔥🌅 GOODBYE SUMMER, HELLO FALL: TORONTO ISLAND BONFIRE 🌅🔥
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🔥🌅 GOODBYE SUMMER, HELLO FALL: TORONTO ISLAND BONFIRE 🌅🔥

### Fire, Food, Music & One Last Summer Night by the Lake

Summer has to end eventually — so why not send it off properly?
Join us on **Toronto Island** for an evening bonfire at Olympic Island as we say goodbye to summer and welcome the beginning of fall.
We’ll take the ferry across together, settle in by the fire, enjoy some food and music, roast marshmallows, and spend the evening relaxing by the water with the Toronto skyline in the background.

This isn't a walk.
It isn't a tour.

It's a **social evening designed to give us time to actually sit around, talk, laugh, eat, and connect with one another.**
Whether you've been coming to the group for years or this is your first event, this is a chance to slow down and enjoy the people around you.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

## 🔥 THE PLAN

We'll meet at the ferry terminal and take the ferry together to Toronto Island.
Once we arrive, we'll make our way over to **Olympic Island**, where our fire pit will be waiting.

We'll have:
🔥 A bonfire
🌭 Hot dogs — including vegetarian options
🍡 Marshmallows for roasting
🎶 Music
🌆 Beautiful views of the Toronto skyline
🗣️ Plenty of time to sit, talk and socialize
The goal is simple:
**Come for the fire.**
**Stay for the food.**

**Leave with a few more people you know.** 🔥💛

## 🚢 FERRY INFORMATION — PLEASE READ

The **fall ferry schedule has not been released yet**, so the ferry departure and return times listed below are **subject to change**.
I will update the event as soon as the official fall schedule is available.

### Current tentative schedule:

📍 **Meetup:** 5:00 PM
🚢 **Ferry:** Approximately 5:20 PM
🔥 **Bonfire:** Olympic Island
🚢 **Return ferry:** Approximately 9:00 PM

**Please do not make other plans around these ferry times until the fall schedule has been confirmed.**

Once the schedule is released, the event page will be updated with the exact times.

## 🧢 MEETUP DETAILS

📍 **Inside the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal, near the bathrooms**
You must enter the ferry terminal and have your ferry ticket **scanned before entering the waiting area**.
Once you're inside the terminal, head toward the **bathrooms**.
🫎 I'll be wearing my Moose Hat.

**PLEASE BE ON TIME.**

The ferry will not wait for us, and I will not be able to hold up the group while waiting for late arrivals.

## 🎟️ FERRY TICKET

You are responsible for purchasing your own ferry ticket.
**Ferry fare:** To be confirmed once the fall schedule and current fare are released.

👉 **[Click Here for Ferry Tickets](https://secure.toronto.ca/FerryTicketOnline/tickets2/index.jsp)**

# 💵 MEETUP FEE — PLEASE READ BEFORE RSVPING

The meetup fee for this event is **$10**.
Payment must be made by **e-transfer to:**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**

### Payment is required within 24 hours of signing up.

This applies to **everyone**.

It does not matter whether you have been a member for one week, one year, or ten years. It does not matter whether you are a long-standing member or a member in good standing.
**Everyone attending this event pays the $10 meetup fee.**
There are no exceptions.

Your payment helps cover:
🔥 Fire permit
🪵 Firewood
🌭 Hot dogs and buns
🍡 Marshmallows
🎶 Music
🥄 Shared roasting supplies

**If payment is not received within 24 hours, your RSVP will be removed so someone else can take the spot.**

## ⚠️ RSVP COMMITMENT

Please only RSVP if you genuinely intend to attend.

**When you sign up, you must also answer all of the event questions.**
This information helps me plan the food, fire and logistics for the evening.

Please don't RSVP simply because the event looks interesting and then decide later whether you feel like coming.

If you aren't sure you can attend, **please wait until you know before signing up.**

Once you've committed, please respect that commitment.

## 🍴 WHAT YOUR $10 INCLUDES

Your meetup fee includes:

*City permit and fire-related costs
- Firewood
*Hot dogs and buns
- Vegetarian hot dog option
*Sauces and condiments
- Marshmallows
*Music
- Shared roasting sticks

**Bring your own drinks.**

## 🎒 WHAT TO BRING

🥤 Your own drinks

🪑 Folding chair or blanket
🧥 A sweater or jacket — September evenings can get cool
🍪 Something small to share if you'd like
🎲 **A game to share** — bring one along if you'd like and feel free to get a group together to play
🔥 Your own roasting stick if you have one
📱 Your phone/camera
Dogs are welcome as long as they are well behaved and permitted in the area.

## 🌧️ WEATHER

This event is planned as an outdoor bonfire and will happen in most weather conditions.
If severe weather or unsafe conditions make the event impossible, the event may be cancelled or rescheduled.
Please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

## 🌈 THE POINT OF THE EVENING

This is a social event.
The bonfire is really just the **container**.
The important part is what happens around it — sitting together, talking to someone you've never met, catching up with people you already know, sharing food, laughing, and maybe making a connection that continues long after the fire goes out.
That's what this group is really about.

We also organize:
🎬 Movies
🚶 Walks & hikes
🎭 Arts & culture
🍽️ Restaurant outings
🎉 Social events
There's always something happening.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email:
📧 **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

### 🔥 Come for the bonfire.

### 🌭 Stay for the food.

### 🌅 Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.

**Let's give summer the send-off it deserves.** 💛🔥

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

***Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events***

*Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate*

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

@tjex.ca

Feel free to follow us!

See Toronto’s Humber River like you’ve never seen it before!

Enter Toronto’s calm, meandering Humber River at King’s Mill Park North. We paddle down as the full moon guides our way to the mouth of Lake Ontario and towards a beautiful view of Toronto’s skyline! We will have staff on the water in their own safety boats during this night time paddle!

*Events are subject to weather and other factors out of our control. If we must cancel or delay an event we will those booked on the [torontoadventures.ca](http://torontoadventures.ca/) website know as soon as possible.*

**Pricing (per seat), Payable online through:** [https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/](https://torontoadventures.ca/all-adventures/full-moon-guided-tour/)
Single Kayak (seats 1 person) : $64.95 +taxes
Tandem Kayak (seats 2 people) : $99.95 +taxes
Regular Canoe (seats 2 people) : $89.95 +taxes
Large Canoe (seats 3 people) : $99.95 +taxes
Voyageur Group (Per person) : $54.95 +taxes

**What's Included:**

* Boat(s)
* Paddle(s)
* PFD(s)/ "Life Jacket(s)”
* Coast Guard Safety Kit.
* Our friendly staff to help you every step of the way!

**What to Bring:**

* Dress for the weather!
* We recommend securely fastened footwear (footwear is not required for SUPs).
* It gets cooler at night so bring an extra layer!
* A water bottle
* Government Issued Photo ID.

**More Information:**

* Anyone under 18 must be accompanied on the water by an adult or legal guardian.
* Waivers Mandatory – sign the online waiver (available through order confirmation) for each attendee.
* We Start & Finish this event at our Humber Location, so no need for a shuttle.
* Please arrive at least 15 minutes early for Check-In to ensure that you get out on time and can paddle for the full 2 hours.
* Paddlers must be comfortable treading water while wearing a PFD and reaching a shoreline (minimum 20 metres to shore).

We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Sounds from Iran, mixed with sounds from Peru. Instruments and artists--they communicate with each other so well!

We love the **Alliance Francaise** space (music, theatre, film, art)

**A World Music Concert--**

**Duo Perse-Inca returns** to Alliance Française Toronto nearly four years after their acclaimed Spadina Theatre performance.

Weekends, we go to Havana, where the vibrant rhythms ignite our souls and live music, dance lessons, & skillful DJs make it a perfect night!

title: "The Meaning of Connection, sponsored by TD"
location: Union, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, Canada
description:
Discover new artwork by Alanah Jewell on Union’s facade banners and in the Front Street Vitrine. 
Union Presents 
The Meaning of Connection 
Sponsored by TD 
  
The Meaning of Connection speaks to how something so small can hold an entire universe of meaning. We often pass a single flower and admire its beauty without thinking about its value; if you magnify that flower, you can see that it is intricately connected to the rest of Creation. The flower is food for the bee, who is a pollinator for plants in a different territory, that are food for the rabbits, who are food for the foxes, who eat the berries that are shaded by the trees, that are homes to the birds, that migrate south and create more life each year, bringing beauty and songs for our southern relatives. That single flower, like each living being, is immensely important. We all have our own version of the flower that helps us stay intricately connected to each other. 
The Meaning of Connection depicts the way Sky Domes are an entire universe for Haudenosaunee. Sky Domes have become a universal motif, often seen on a smaller scale, yet representing such great beliefs: our connection to Sky World, the physical world, our Creation story, our medicines, foods, lands, water, the sun, the moon, our stories, our teachings, and our ancestors.  Traditionally, the Sky Dome is identified by its dome shape with swirling, celestial trees, often repeated in a pattern and with other elements like water, medicines, land and more. Sky Domes often line the borders of our skirts, appear in our beadwork and regalia, and are a central piece of art in our homes and on our bodies. 
For the vitrine, I wanted to honour the way we have traditionally displayed Sky Domes and created a universal emblem that connects all Haudenosaunee to each other. This piece pays homage to the ancestors that took an entire way of life and found a single symbol to represent everything that matters, existing for millennia as a central piece of who we are, and have become a symbol that we each wear with pride. 
For the outdoor banners, I wanted to show what the Sky Dome represents on a magnified scale. Here, you see a single Sky Dome in the background, with life flowing in and out. This is meant to represent how a single Sky Dome is boundless, representing so much, for so long, and for so many beings. It tells a single story about bears spending time by a river, with swallows flying above, during a beautiful summer sunset. These beings exist in harmony amongst the plants, the medicines, the rolling hills and the sky. What would each Sky Dome look like if we stopped for a moment and zoomed in? 
My hope for The Meaning of Connection is for each of us to bring meaning to everything; to see how important, valued, and indispensable life is. Like the Sky Dome, or the flower, we all have a place in Creation, in our stories and in our future. 
About the Artist 
Alanah Astehtsi Otsistohkwa (Morningstar) Jewell (she/her) is a mixed First Nations artist. She is proudly Bear Clan from Oneida Nation of the Thames, grew up off-reserve and currently lives in Kitchener, Ontario. Alanah is a passionate illustrator, painter and muralist, and appreciates all forms of art, challenging herself to try every form. Her career is one for her many passions: the intersection of nature, expression, community and joy is her favourite place to be. 
Her work is often described as symmetrical, colourful and soft. She works to create vast worlds through her artwork that feel safe and calm, and strives to show how nature can feel when you create a friendship with her. An avid animal lover, she feels deep love, passion and empathy for all living beings; they are not just her subjects, but the life source of her work, and her biggest inspiration. 
About Union 
Union is honoured to present this exhibition by artist Alanah Jewell, whose work deeply aligns with our programming vision of celebrating creativity, inclusion, and civic connection. We are proud to highlight voices of Indigenous Peoples in our year-round programming, especially in recognition of National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. With the support of organizations like the Gord Downie & Chanie Wenjack Fund and TD, we are grateful to create space for meaningful dialogue and reflection through Alanah’s powerful artistic lens. 
As a proud Legacy Spaces partner with the Gord Downie and Chanie Wenjack Fund, we are continuing to use our public space to take reconciliACTION. 
About TD 
We recognize art from the Indigenous community is made of diverse forms and holds different meanings that can create conversations about the past, present, and future. TD has been highlighting artists from Indigenous communities since 1967 through the TD Gallery of Indigenous Art  and is committed to advancing Truth and Reconciliation by amplifying diverse voices that leverage the power of art as a means to learn more about the historical and ongoing contributions of Indigenous Peoples in Canada. Learn more about how TD is  working together with Indigenous Communities at td.com/indigenous.

For more information about Union’s programming visit torontounion.ca

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Friday
* Saturday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🌿🚶 LEASIDE SPUR TRAIL, WILKET CREEK & EDWARDS GARDENS WALK (10KM) 🚶🌿
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🌿🚶 **LEASIDE SPUR TRAIL, WILKET CREEK & EDWARDS GARDENS WALK (10KM)** 🚶🌿

Forest Trails, Flowing Creeks & A Spring Garden Pause
Some of the best parts of Toronto don’t feel like the city at all.
Join us for a longer, energizing social walk through some of the city’s most scenic green spaces — from quiet trails to winding creeks, with a beautiful stop at the gardens along the way.

We’ll explore the Leaside Spur Trail, connect into the peaceful paths of Wilket Creek Park, and make our way toward Edwards Gardens — where you’ll have time to wander, take in the seasonal blooms, and enjoy a little moment of calm in the middle of the walk.
This is not a formal tour.

It’s a social, active walk with great scenery and even better company.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

🚶‍♂️ What We’ll Do

We’ll begin at McDonald’s and head onto the Leaside Spur Trail, easing into the walk before connecting with Wilket Creek’s forested paths.
From there, we’ll continue toward Sunnybrook Park and into Edwards Gardens, where we’ll take a relaxed break so you can explore, enjoy the flowers, and recharge.
After our stop, we’ll loop back along the trails, returning to our starting point.

Once we’re back, those who want can grab an ice cream at D Spot Desserts for a well-earned creamy dessert. 🥪
No pressure to join — totally optional.

***

🌦️ Weather & Expectations

This walk will happen in typical Toronto conditions — including cold, light rian, or damp trails.
Please come prepared for a full 10KM walk with some hills.
Good footwear is essential.
.
Also — this is NOT a guided or historical tour. I’ll share bits along the way, but the focus is on movement, nature, and connection.

***

🧢 Meetup Details

📍 Meetup Location: Outside McDonald’s
🫎 I’ll be wearing my Moose Hat
⏰ Meetup Time: 11:00 AM
I will only wait 5 minutes.
Early is on time.
On time is late.

We’ll begin promptly and won’t be able to track late arrivals — thank you for understanding.
End point: Back at McDonald’s

***

🎟️ Meetup Fee: $5 cash in person or e-transfer to
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This helps support the group and allows us to keep hosting events like this. Thank you for supporting community! 💖

***

🎒 What to Bring

Water or a warm drink
Good walking shoes (trails may be uneven or muddy)
A snack
Weather-appropriate clothing (layers are key!)

Optional: cash/card if joining for lunch
Please also use the washroom before arriving, as stops are limited.

***

🌈 Who Is This For?

This group is open to anyone who wants to be social and make friends — whether single or not.
We also host:
🎬 Movies
🚶 Walks & hikes
🎭 Arts & culture outings
🍽️ Restaurant gatherings

There’s always something happening.

***

REMEMBER: You’re welcome to just show up on the day if you’re unsure about your schedule.
And as always, sometimes plans shift and events may need to be canceled — please keep an eye on updates.

***

👤 Organizer: Mathew
Questions? Post on the event wall or email
📧 torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com

Come for the trails. Stay for the gardens.
Leave feeling like you escaped the city — without ever leaving it. 🌿✨

title: Ireland Park, Queen's Wharf, and 1847 Irish Potato Famine
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

This special historical walking tour discusses the Irish Potato Famine in great detail, and the implications for Toronto in 1847.

Starting the walking tour near Ireland Park just east of Bathurst Quay we take a deep dive into the events that saw thousands of people head west to Toronto in 1847! A truly global event! A life changing event for those caught up in the famine in Ireland and Toronto itself. Toronto was never the same after, and impacted the future of the city for nearly a century.

But the stories surrounding Ireland Park are not the only stories from this era. This tour looks at the Potato Famine with a different lens. We end at the corner of King and John streets at the site of the Fever Sheds.

This extensive tour begins in **Little Norway Park** adjacent to Queen's Quay West, at the foot of Bathurst Street, and ends at King Street and John Street!

This tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season.

This walk has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

description:
À la croisée des voies ferrées  La naissance de The Junction 1ère partie  
Départ : À l’angle sud-ouest des rues Keele & Dundas West, (servi par les autobus de la rue Keele #89 et #41 et/ou le bus de la rue Dundas ouest #40.
Arrivée : Même endroit
Guides : Wafa Smiai – Rolande Smith

Il y a 130 ans, The Junction n’était pas un simple quartier de Toronto, mais une municipalité indépendante : West Toronto Junction. Venez découvrir le patrimoine bâti de ce carrefour symbolique, dont les rues ont été tracées selon la logique de trois grandes lignes de chemin de fer se rejoignant à la fin du XIXème siècle. Ce croisement a donné naissance à l’un des secteurs les plus riches en histoire de l’ouest de la ville.

Le projet de Loi 23 intitulée Projet de loi 23, Loi de 2022 visant à accélérer la construction de plus de logements (More Homes Built Faster Act), constitue un véritable défi pour la préservation de ce patrimoine commercial, industriel et résidentiel exceptionnel. 
Cette1ere visite constitue la première partie du thème consacré à The Junction, se concentrera sur son corridor commercial et son patrimoine résidentiel.  La 2nde visite,  planifiée pour le samedi 14 novembre, se concentrera sur le paysage industriel historique de The Junction Triangle (réservez la date, les détails suivront plus tard).

Historitours 2026 – pas nécessaire de réserver. La SHT passe le chapeau à la fin de la visite, merci.  Pas de chien  Contacts : info@sht.ca

Toronto et son alimentation : Héritage, actualité, défis et possibilités
Départ : Près de l’entrée à Wychwood Barns, au 601, rue Christie (2 rues au sud de St. Clair, desservi par le tram 512 et l’autobus Christie 126). 
Arrivée : Retour au même endroit. 
Guides : Yasmina Bahlil et Paul Overy. 
Et si vous découvriez Toronto à travers ce qui nourrit ses habitants depuis des siècles? Cette visite guidée vous plongera dans l’histoire de l’agriculture et des aliments qui ont façonné la ville. Du maïs et autres aliments cultivés par les Premières Nations aux premières fermes des colons, en passant par les marchés publics, jardins communautaires et l’arrivée de nouvelles cultures alimentaires, explorez comment les produits de la terre et des eaux ont accompagné et permis le développement de Toronto. Une balade enrichissante pour comprendre l’histoire alimentaire de la ville et son avenir possible… une bouchée pédestre à la fois! 
Cette visite aura lieu surtout sur des trottoirs et autres espaces plats, avec quelques pentes mais pas d’escaliers. La marche sera d’environ 2 km, sur une période de 2 heures. Quelques bancs en cours de route. Toilettes au début et à la fin. 
Pas besoin de réserver – Visite guidée gratuite 
La Société d’histoire de Toronto passe le chapeau à la fin. Pas de chien.

title: The Invincible - Stanisław Lem
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody,

September's pick was just as popular as *Blindsight* on our survey. Our outer-space mystery series continues with our highest-voted classic in a while, Stanisław Lem's eponymous *The Invincible* is supposed to be a wild ride.

As a reminder, we skip our October book each year to highlight the [Brooklyn SciFi Film Festival](https://brooklynscififilmfest.com/). The BSFFF is back for its 7th installment, with films streaming online and screening in person throughout the week. I'll share more information about the different events and ways to participate in September. I hope you'll join us!

Book of the Month
*The Invincible* \- Stanisław Lem \(1964\)

*The Invincible* is considered one of Stanisław Lem's defining novels and another true classic of science fiction. We're back aboard a starship this month, following a crew sent to investigate the disappearance of an expedition on a distant planet. It's a mystery wrapped in world-building, atmospheric exploration, and the kind of ideas that made Lem such an influential voice in the genre.

Book Club has really enjoyed the Lem stories we've read so far, can't wait to dive into one of the novels that put him on the map. Ursula K. Le Guin said about *The Invincible*: "Anybody who likes a mystery will find it here — and its solution."

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

title: Toronto Language Exchange | Practice Spanish & English (In-Person)
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
Join our **Spanish–English Language Exchange Meetup** and improve your conversation skills in a relaxed, social environment. This free event is perfect for anyone looking to practice Spanish or English while meeting new people in a cozy coffee shop setting.

### **🗣️ What You’ll Do**

* Practice Spanish and English through real conversations
* Join small groups and switch languages throughout the event
* Learn practical vocabulary and everyday expressions
* Build confidence speaking in a supportive environment

### **👥 Who Should Attend**

* Spanish learners (all levels)
* English learners (all levels)
* Native speakers who want to help others
* Anyone interested in language exchange and cultural connection

### **☕ Venue**

We meet at a local coffee shop—just grab a drink and enjoy the conversation!

### **💸 Cost**

**FREE event** (please support the venue by purchasing a drink)

### **🌟 Why Join?**

Language exchanges are one of the most effective ways to learn. You’ll improve faster by speaking with real people, hearing authentic accents, and using the language in everyday situations.
Whether you're a beginner or fluent speaker, you’ll find a welcoming community ready to practice and connect.

**👉 RSVP now and start speaking with confidence!**

location: Toronto Reference Library, Activity Room (Youth Hub, First Floor)
description:
This program provides a supportive, low-pressure environment where newcomers can build confidence in their English writing, communication, and presentation skills. Together, we will:
1. Have a short, collective discussion period.
2. Begin writing based on a prompt from the instructor

title: Fat Fables: Resisting Fatphobia and Finding Fat Joy
location: Parkdale
description:
Join artists, Jules Vodarek Hunter and Morgan Davis, co-creators of
Fat Fables
, for an evening of learning, performance and making connections.
Fat Fables
is a performance and creation program for Fat Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans, Queer, Intersex, Asexual (2SLGBTQIA+) folks. The facilitators will share its positive impact in celebrating and uplifting different bodies, discuss the origins of fatphobia and how it shapes the current state of affairs on all bodies today.
Photo Credit: Jae Yang
A brief excerpt from the book, Belly of the Beast: the Politics of Anti-fatness as Anti-blackness by Da'Shaun Harrison, will be read to spark an open conversation. With size-inclusive seating and cozy welcoming vibes, the facilitators will lead a creative writing session, where attendees can write, share, and participate as much or as little as they want.
The goal of Fat Fables is to create community for fat queer and trans folks, to tell stories, and to dream of a fat future where we all thrive. Fat people deserve to be visible, to be seen and to be artists on stage.
The program aims to help attendees feel empowered, supported, and to leave with a full heart.

Free. Doors open for registrants at 5:45 pm. At 6:00 pm, spots become first-come, first-served until capacity is reached. The program will run from 6 pm to 8 pm.

The story unfolds as Victor Joseph and another young man from the Indian reservation, Thomas Builds-the-Fire, set off to collect Arnold Joseph's pick-up truck and ashes from Arizona after Arnold has died. title: Percussion Basics with LMMS
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor - eLearning Lab
description:
Odd-time beatmaking and sampling basics using Linux MultiMedia Studio & Audacity.
Linux MultiMedia Studio is a digital audio workstation, or DAW. It is a sound generation system, synthesizer, beat/bassline editor and MIDI control system that can power a small home music studio. Sounds, tones and rhythms can be generated, played, and artfully arranged to create entire tracks. Tracks can then be layered to create songs, which can later be saved to an output format.
This percussion workshop is divided into two separate sections:
Odd-time beatmaking
Sampling basics using Linux MultiMedia Studio + Audacity
An odd, irregular or unequal subdivision of a beat can be difficult to play but do have patterns that are discernable for the performer. The most common irregular metres mix simple time (whose basic note division is in groups of two), and compound time (threes) together within a single measure. Odd-time polyrhythms commonly appear in Latin, West African and other musical genres.
A sample is the use of a portion of an existing song, recontextualized for a substantially new recording such as a drumbeat. The point is to make a new original track using a sample from a previous song. Sampling has its historical roots in tape-looping, turntablism (DJing) and drum machines, and can be heard in avant-garde, Hip Hop and other genres.
Keyboarding and mouse skills are required.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: From Tribal Knowledge to Code: Custom Skills for GitHub Copilot Modernization
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Every application contains business rules, architectural patterns, internal frameworks, and development standards that generic AI cannot fully understand.

Without that context, modernization efforts can produce inconsistent results and require significant manual review.

Learn how GitHub Copilot Modernization custom skills help organizations bring their institutional knowledge directly into the modernization process.

See how custom skills can encode business logic, software factory patterns, and governance requirements to generate more consistent, accurate, and production-ready outcomes across applications and teams. Through a live demonstration, you'll see how custom skills transform modernization workflows by turning tribal knowledge into reusable guidance that scales across projects.

Join us to learn how to preserve organizational expertise while accelerating application modernization with AI.

Key Takeaway: Custom skills help organizations modernize faster while ensuring AI-generated changes align with their unique standards, practices, and business requirements.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
location: Palmerston, Meeting Room
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.

title: ROTMAN Talk:  Prof. Daron Acemoglu- "What Happened to Liberal Democracy?" ($25)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
### **Book Synopsis:**

**From Daron Acemoglu, 2024 Nobel laureate in economics and coauthor of *Why Nations Fail,* an ambitious and expansive inquiry into the biggest story in global politics over the last hundred years: the rise and fall of liberal democracy.**

**"A very important work and a must-read."** —Thomas Piketty, #1 *New York Times* bestselling author of *Capital in the Twenty-First Century*

**Tickets are $25 only (or with book $44). LINK below.**

**"Daron Acemoglu is one of the most brilliant and insightful thinkers I’ve ever known. His particular genius is being able to look at impossibly complex problems and see right to the heart of what matters. This book is a tour de force that left me feeling more optimistic about the future than I have in a long time."**

—Steven Levitt, #1 *New York Times* bestselling author of *Freakonomics*

The dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991 raised hopes that we were one step closer to the triumph of liberalism. Soon, many predicted, we would all be living in functional liberal democracies. Sustained economic growth would benefit all segments of society and war would be a relic of the past. A generation later, one can only ask: What happened?

**Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu** argues in this powerful book that liberal democracy flourished when it pursued its core promises of shared prosperity, democratic governance, and the free pursuit of knowledge. But liberalism, a philosophy built to challenge power, never fully adjusted to becoming the establishment. Nor was it able to deal with the economic and social disruptions that digital technologies wrought. Worse, in the postindustrial economy, liberalism turned its back on its core promises. As a segment of college-educated elites became politically dominant and separated from the rest of society, they sowed the seeds of widespread inequality while intensifying efforts to reshape mass culture and values.

title: In Depth Sewing Intro - Sept 29 [Tuesdays - 6 week program]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
LEARN TO SEW 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Suitable for beginners. This class goes over the basics of operating a sewing machine, cutting and sewing garments, and basic pattern alterations. 
 
 
 The main project for this class is an apron custom fit to YOU. A typical first project is a tote bag,but we’ve chosen to have our students make an apron as it covers the same skills while also teaching basic tailoring and fitting. The goal of this class is to provide students with the basic skills associated with sewing, understanding patterns, and textiles, while promoting confidence and shifting the mindset of your everyday clothing as things that suit your needs and body, rather than things to simply wear. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 This class will also explore clothing repairs and minor alterations like hemming, altering
necklines, adding pockets, etc. Students are encouraged to bring in items they wish to alter or repair. 
 
 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 
 
 

 
 Schedule 
6 weeks, Tuesdays 6pm to 9pm 
 
 

 
 
 Outcomes 
 At the end of the course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- Proficiency with operating a sewing machine safely 

- Understanding of fabric types, their uses, how to prep them for sewing, and how to cut fabric 

- Comfort with taking measurements of the body and how to apply them to a pattern 

- Knowledge of basic pattern alterations and how to adjust existing garments to fit you better 

- Understanding of how to transfer patterns to fabric so that space is used as efficiently as possible 

- Understanding of pinning and ironing techniques 

- Familiarity with basic sewing techniques including seams, hemming, hand stitching,
applying pockets, fasteners including buttons, zippers, snaps, and ties, as well as
different stitch uses for different techniques and materials

- Basic repairs like fixing holes, torn seams, holes in pockets, adding patches

- Basic alterations like adjusting hems, changing necklines, switching out buttons or other fasteners

, the film fuses present-day scenes with re-enactments and archival footage of his young years of displacement and addiction, and takes us on an inspiring journey to the space beyond, and to the spaces between us all.

title: ABCD Reads "Country People" by Daniel Mason
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads "**[Country People](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4758420)**" by Daniel Mason.

[[RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5996722009669632) of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Daniel Mason’s latest novel sees him return to the verdant New England landscape that so captivated readers of 2023’s acclaimed North Woods. This time, though, he hops the border from Massachusetts into Vermont – and effects a deeper shift in the process. Where North Woods was a foray into history, telling the tale of a house and its inhabitants over three centuries, in Country People Mason turns his attention to literature and mines the rich seams of text, from myths to Milton to Shakespeare to Tolstoy and all points in between, that make up his novel’s foundations. This is, at its core, a story about stories; a tale about the tales we tell each other, and our children, and ourselves." (from [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/jul/07/country-people-by-daniel-mason-review-a-joyful-follow-up-to-north-woods))

"Miles Krzelewski is a devoted husband, a doting father beloved for his outlandish bedtime stories, and the proud owner of a truffle-hunting dog in a land with no truffles. He is also a bit lost, twelve years late with his PhD on Russian folktales, and increasingly haunted by a sense that he's become a disappointment to his family. So when his wife Kate accepts a visiting professorship at a prestigious college in the far away forests of Vermont, he decides that this will be his year to finally move forward with his life. [...] Joyous, absurd, and life-affirming, Country People is a luminous exploration of marriage and parenthood, the nature of belief and the power of stories, and the ways in which we find connection in an increasingly fragmented world." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/242518677-country-people))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Civic Meetup #562: Ban the Kid, Keep their Data
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
description:
New technologies and organizations’ practices are regularly placing pressures and challenges on our privacy and transparency rights. This month, Civic Tech Toronto and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario are highlighting the work to defend, enforce, explain and update these rights. To see all September events, check our events listing on Guild. 

‎‎

Topic: Ban the Kid, Keep their Data

Governments in Canada and abroad are moving to protect children online: banning kids from social media, mandating safer defaults, restricting what platforms can recommend to young users. Much of it depends on first establishing how old users are. In this talk, Sara Grimes looks at the infrastructure these proposals routinely require, including AI-driven facial estimation and behavioural inference, applied to everyone, collecting more data from children in the name of protecting them. She'll ask what the evidence says about whether these technologies work and what their spreading implementation means for children’s privacy and other rights.

‎‎

Speaker: Sara M. Grimes, PhD \[joining remotely]

Sara Grimes is a full professor in Communication Studies at McGill University, where she holds the Wolfe Chair in Scientific and Technological Literacy and directs the Kids Play Tech Lab. For over two decades she has tracked how digital games and social media platforms collect data from young users, and how policy and design decisions quietly shape what rights children get to exercise. She's the author of Digital Playgrounds (University of Toronto Press, 2021) and co-author of the CIFAR policy brief Responsible AI and Children. She regularly works with policymakers in Canada and internationally on children’s privacy. // LinkedIn / kidsplaytech.com

title: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea: Emily Wilson on Translating Antiquity
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Renowned classicist and translator Emily Wilson explores the art and challenges of bringing ancient literature to modern readers.
In Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea, Emily Wilson — whose acclaimed renditions of Homer's Odyssey and Iliad have captured a generation's imagination — takes readers on a sharp and often entertaining tour through antiquity. Drawing on twenty years of scholarship and teaching, Wilson illuminates the difficult choices translators must make, the pleasures of finding new solutions to old problems, and the inevitable frustrations of never fully capturing what lives in the original text.
Across chapters ranging from the politics of Helen of Troy to the obscenities of Aristophanes, from Roman imitation of Greek models to contemporary debates over "foreignizing" and "domesticizing" styles, Wilson examines how modern norms of gender, sexuality, violence, humor, and power complicate our readings of ancient works—and how translation always risks denaturing what is unique and strange about the ancient world.
Brilliant, erudite, and accessible to readers with no classical background, Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea is at once an introduction to the wonders of Greek and Roman literature, a manifesto for the value of translation in a rapidly changing world, and an invitation to encounter ancient cultures anew.
Emily Wilson speaks with Ella Street about Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea and the lifelong work of carrying ancient voices into the present.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

description:

Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: Pay What You Wish (Free, $10, $20, $30)

Honouring the experiences of Residential School survivors, join us for an intimate and insightful conversation with Ojibwe Kwe author, educator, and Residential School survivor, Karen Chaboyer, to commemorate Orange Shirt Day and National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. Tea and bannock will be provided by Candace’s Catering.  
Agenda
6:30 pm – Doors open
7:00 pm – Conversation begins
8:00 pm – Conversation ends, Open dialogue and visiting
9:00 pm – Museum closes 
RSVP  
ABOUT KAREN CHABOYER: 
 
Karen Chaboyer is an Ojibwe kwe, a great-grandmother, a grandmother, and mother. She is also an author, a public speaker, and an educator. Karen is from Rainy River First Nation, a community in Northwestern Ontario, Treaty 3 Territory. Karen is a survivor of St. Margaret’s Indian Residential School, also known as the Fort Frances Indian Residential School where she attended for 9 years. Karen was born into a family of 11 siblings: 9 brothers and 2 sisters. She is the third youngest in her family. She is also a second generation survivor of Residential School. Karen has been presenting since 2006. Her audiences are mostly elementary/high schools, colleges, universities and organizations. Karen shares the effects Residential School had on her and how she lost her identity, her roots, her culture and language. Karen’s goal is to educate people on the impact Residential Schools had on her and Indigenous individuals, families and communities to this day.

title: Queer Death Salon: Grief Gardening
location: Online, online
description: In times of grief, many people find that a connection to land, earth, and the tending of life can help carry us through. It is well established that a connection to nature, no matter how small, helps improve our experiences of depression, anxiety, and sense of wellbeing. Pulling from their their personal experiences, Eli will lead participants in a discussion about; the history of Grief Gardening through various cultural perspectives gardening as a tool for emotional processing and providing a sense of control and purpose creating sites for remembrance tending to a relationship with nature to encourage a sense of hope and renewal He will also support participants with ideas about how to get started or expand on our grief gardens. Eli (they/he) is a gardener and former landscaper, wetlands restorationist and wildlife biologist currently living on Ohlone land in Oakland. Mutual aid, covid realism, disability justice, queerness and art as well as gardening all help them with the little and big sources of grief that life brings us. ‍

title: Let's Learn GitHub Copilot SDK (Java)
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Join this beginner-friendly livestream to learn how to build agentic applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK for Java, without implementing the agent loop yourself. Unlike calling a model API directly, the SDK gives your application programmatic access to Copilot’s agent runtime, including conversation management, planning, tool orchestration, streaming events, and session state. During the session, we’ll explore clients, sessions, prompts, and the agent runtime. You’ll learn how to create multi-turn conversations, stream responses in real time, expose application functions as tools, connect external capabilities through MCP servers, and control agent behavior with hooks and permission handlers. We’ll also help you understand when to use the Copilot SDK instead of the interactive Copilot CLI: use the CLI for developer tasks in the terminal, and use the SDK when you want to embed Copilot’s agentic capabilities in your own application or service. No prior experience with the GitHub Copilot SDK is required.

title: When One Agent Isn't Enough: Orchestrating Secure Parallel Agent Swarms
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
AI agents need to run code, call APIs, and fan out in parallel - but doing that safely at scale is hard.

This session shows how to build agentic workloads on hardware-isolated, sub-second, disposable compute that agents can provision themselves. Watch a live research-agent swarm spin up a fleet of secure sandboxes in parallel, run real work in true isolation, and tear it down automatically - with keyless auth throughout.

Powered by Azure Container Apps Sandboxes. You'll learn
• Why untrusted agent code and multi-agent fan-out break traditional container/VM approaches
• The pattern for safe, ephemeral, per-agent compute: isolation, instant start, scale-to-zero, snapshot/resume
• How agents can self-provision compute as a tool to extend their own capabilities
• Controlling blast radius with hardware isolation, egress policies, and keyless managed identity
• A working orchestration pattern for parallel agent swarms you can adapt to your own workloads

[Explore the Build Cloud Native Apps series](https://developer.microsoft.com/reactor/series/S-1692?wt.mc_id=meetup_27397_webpage_reactor)

title: Decadence and Seventy Book Launch
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Biblioasis and Random House Canada, for a double book launch, featuring both Richard Kelly Kemmick and Ian Brown.
About the Books:
Decadence
"The genre of memoir is bullshit (as I humbly posit). No one actually lives like they are moving along some grand Freytag’s triangle. Rather, we live within isolated instances, specific struggles and victories, which, when compiled, form a narrative."—Richard Kelly Kemick.
In
Decadence
, Richard Kelly Kemick’s “accidental memoir of a sort,” the author ranges widely through his myriad preoccupations and obsessions—volleyball, municipal landfills, dogs, high school plays, Christmas villages, love—out of which the shape of a unique sensibility is revealed. Reminiscent of the three Davids—Rakoff, Sedaris, and Wallace—these essays accrete into a portrait of a man trying to make sense of a world in which there are no goddamn rules; and yet one in which every action has sometimes profound consequences.
A book of intelligence and care and kindness and humour and yearning and the occasional epiphany, Decadence gathers up from the odds and ends of living what makes a modern life—quiet and desperate as it may at times be—worth celebrating.
Order a copy of
Decadence
here
Seventy
Ian Brown, award-winning author of The Boy in the Moon and the memoir Sixty, now recounts his daily reckoning with the milestone age of seventy. Fearlessly candid, often funny and relentlessly real, Brown asks the terrifying questions we all have about growing old, even when he doesn’t want to know the answers.
An acclaimed journalist and chronicler of contemporary life, seventy-year-old Ian Brown is not going gently into his eighth decade. The outlook is more perilous than it was at age sixty, but Brown is determined (however hopelessly) not to let time get the better of him.
During the course of his seventy-first year, Brown writes incessantly, travelling on assignment for the Globe and Mail across the United States in the months leading to the shocking 2024 election; holidays with family and friends, always aware he might not see them again; skis and rows and exercises like a madman while turning a wary eye on the live-forever movement; takes up pickleball and talks books; and in general tries (and frequently fails) to show some human courage in the face of the march of his dwindling years.
Along the way he encounters the lists that have suddenly become essential to daily life (what to take when leaving the house, what to pack for a trip, what to pick up at the drugstore); the indignities of medical tests and the shock of financing a retirement; the terrors and pleasures of growing older with one’s spouse of four decades; the now-suspenseful drama of sex; the thrilling spectacle of watching adult children inhabit new roles of familial responsibility; and the shocking new lessons of life as an older person (accept compliments with grace, remember to smile, stand up straighter).
As the percentage of the Canadian population over eighty-five will triple in the next twenty-five years, Brown contemplates his mortality and that of his contemporaries for readers of all ages. Growing old—anything after seventy—is a grave challenge, but also enormously liberating: if there is something you want to say or do, now is your chance to say it or do it. “I have to keep taking chances,” Brown reckons. “I don’t want to give in too soon.”

Seventy

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Sine Lam
location: Forest Hill
description:
Throughout the month of October, works by artist Sine Lam will be on display at the Forest Hill branch.
Sine Lam is an emerging artist currently based in Ontario. She studied Fine Art at St. Lawrence College. Her artistic practice blends symbolism, realism, and surrealism, drawing inspiration from human emotion, urban solitude, connection, memories, nature, and time.
Her series,
Passage of Time
, reflects her experiences of city life and explores themes of contrast and contradiction— visual beauty paired with melancholy, and relaxation alongside loneliness, much like life itself, where joy and sorrow coexist. Her work often carries hidden messages through symbolic elements.
Sine's work has been featured in various group exhibitions, including at the Marianne van Silfhout Gallery.
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during the Forest Hill branch's open hours. Please check the
Forest Hill
branch page before you visit.
Free. All are welcome.
Image credit: Sine Lam; "Back to Silence"; oil.

title: Let's Learn GitHub Copilot SDK (.NET)
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Join this beginner-friendly livestream to learn how to build agentic applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK for .NET, without implementing the agent loop yourself. Unlike calling a model API directly, the SDK gives your application programmatic access to Copilot’s agent runtime, including conversation management, planning, tool orchestration, streaming events, and session state. During the session, we’ll explore clients, sessions, prompts, and the agent runtime. You’ll learn how to create multi-turn conversations, stream responses in real time, expose application functions as tools, connect external capabilities through MCP servers, and control agent behavior with hooks and permission handlers. We’ll also help you understand when to use the Copilot SDK instead of the interactive Copilot CLI: use the CLI for developer tasks in the terminal, and use the SDK when you want to embed Copilot’s agentic capabilities in your own application or service. No prior experience with the GitHub Copilot SDK is required.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.
