title: Engineering leadership: Navigating a changing world
location: Online
description:
Engineering has always addressed challenges by advancing technology. But success now depends not only on technical expertise but also on the ability to connect people, foster collaboration and drive innovation across complex environments.  
What does it take to lead as an engineer in an era defined by AI, global collaboration and rapid change?
Join Professor Emily Moore for an engaging discussion on how engineering careers are evolving and how leaders can adapt to meet new challenges. Drawing on her research into engineering career paths, teamwork and organizational dynamics, Professor Moore will share practical insights on developing the skills that matter for long-term success. Discover how engineers can strengthen their leadership capabilities, navigate change with confidence and amplify their impact in a world where the human side of engineering has never been more important.  
Join us on October 14, 2026 at our monthly Skule™ Lunch & Learn.  
By registering for the Skule™ Lunch & Learn event, you could potentially earn Continuing Professional Development (CPD) credits. CPDs are essential for professional engineers and limited license holders to renew their licenses annually through the PEO PEAK Program. If you’re wondering whether this event offering qualifies you for CPD credits, click here to learn more. 
About the speaker
Professor Emily Moore was appointed Director of Troost Institute for Leadership Education in Engineering (ILead) in October 2018, after more than twenty years in industry. Emily started her career at the Xerox Research Centre of Canada scaling up new materials and processes from the lab to manufacturing. In her 11 years at Xerox, Emily learned a great deal about leading teams and developing new products, becoming a manager and Principal Engineer. Emily then spent 10 years at Hatch, a global engineering firm serving the mining, energy and infrastructure sectors. Emily led international teams to develop new product and service offerings and to deliver major projects, first as the Director of Technology Development and then as Managing Director, Water. Emily was also the inaugural chair of Hatch’s Global Diversity and Inclusion efforts. Emily holds a bachelor’s degree in engineering chemistry from Queen’s University and completed a doctorate in physical chemistry from Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar. In 2016 Emily was recognized as one of 100 Global Inspirational Women in Mining and received the SCI Canada Kalev Pugi Award.

title: Oct 14 - Advances in AI at SDSU
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from AI researchers at San Diego State University.

**Date, Time Location**

Oct 14, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/advances-in-ai-at-sdsu-october-14-2026)**

**Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation**

This talk will introduces how a general-purpose agent can directly drive a physical robot throughout task execution without any task-specific or environment-specific training. We introduce Agent as Policy (AGP), which places task planning and execution under the agent’s control.

*About the Speaker*

[Xiaobai Liu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xiaobai-liu-33598336/) is a Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where he directs the Machine Vision and Perception Lab. Prior to joining SDSU in 2015, he conducted research and taught at UCLA.

**Grounding Multimodal Open-World Learning for Physical AI**

Physical AI systems such as robots, unmanned vehicles, and embodied agents must perceive and reason about a world that is dynamic, unstructured, and rarely matches their training distribution. Yet most multimodal models remain brittle when confronted with novel objects, unseen conditions, and a messy unstructured environment.

This talk develops how grounding perception across modalities and environments can make open-world learning more robust for physically situated systems. Drawing on our recent work, I will highlight the core challenges of multimodal open-world learning including out-of-distribution detection, distribution shift generalization, and cascaded semantic grounding and point toward multimodal systems that stay reliable when deployed in the unpredictable open world.

*About the Speakers*

[Salimeh Sekeh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/salimeh-sekeh-65473344/) is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where she directs the Sekeh Laboratory. Her recognition includes an NSF CAREER Award and a Cisco research gift (both 2022), and the Maine College of Engineering and Computing Early Career Research Award (2023), along with multiple industry and federal research awards.

[Mary Wisell ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mary-isabelle-wisell/)is a second-year PhD student in the Sekeh Lab and leads the lab's work on environment-aware OOD detection and cascaded failure analysis for multimodal intelligence with several publications in top-tier Machine Learning and computer vision conferences.

**Model-Free, Position-Free Signal Source Seeking Using Unmanned Maritime Systems**

Long-range signal source detection in open-world environments presents a significant challenge, mainly due to the detrimental effects of the environment on signals propagation paths and presence of extraneous signal sources. While distributed static sensing systems are often employed, achieving scalability and comprehensive coverage across expansive areas is cost-prohibitive.

One affordable solution involves using low-cost autonomous unmanned vehicles (AUVs) that can leverage their mobility and actively explore the environment using extremum seeking control (ESC) algorithms. This talk presents novel ESC approaches to steer AUVs to sources of interest in an a priori unknown, highly non-convex map.

*About the Speaker*

[Zahra Nili Ahmadabadi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zahra-nili-ahmadabadi-phd-29113171) is Associate Professor with the Mechanical Engineering Department at San Diego State University (SDSU). She is a recipient of the ASME rising star award and ARO Early career award.

title: Open Studio: Justin Peck’s Partita
location: West Wing, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, M5R 1V9, Canada
description:
With Open Studio, Union and Fall for Dance North invite you into the daily life of a dancer. If you’re passing through Union Station’s West Wing, pause for a moment or stay for an hour and experience the artists at work. 
From 12–2 PM, witness the cast of Partita prepare to take the stage in HEAR THE DANCE: Signature Programme 3. This open rehearsal of Justin Peck’s sneaker ballet invites you to get closer to the artists as they move through technically challenging choreography that celebrates the joy of being together. 
The rehearsal features recent graduates of Toronto Metropolitan University and students from the National Ballet School. 
Justin Peck is a three-time Tony Award-winning director, choreographer, filmmaker, and dancer based in New York City. He is the Resident Choreographer of the New York City Ballet and only the second person in the institution’s 75-year history to hold this title. 
He has created more than 50 stage and theatre works presented around the world, including at Lincoln Center, the Palais Garnier, Sydney Opera House, Brooklyn Academy of Music, and Broadway. His creations have been performed by companies including the Paris Opera Ballet, Australian Ballet, Dresden Semperoper Ballet, Hong Kong Ballet, Boston Ballet, Juilliard, The National Ballet of Canada, Miami City Ballet, Pacific Northwest Ballet, LA Dance Project, Dutch National Ballet, the School of American Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, and Houston Ballet. 
Co-presented by Union and Fall for Dance North.

title: Open Studio: Esie Mensah’s ZAYO
location: Union, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, Canada
description:
With Open Studio, Union and Fall for Dance North invite you into the daily life of a dancer. If you’re passing through Union Station’s West Wing, pause for a moment or stay for an hour and experience the artists at work. 
From 4–7 PM, experience Toronto-based dancer and choreographer Esie Mensah in process as she rehearses ZAYO with her company of dancers. 
ZAYO is an Afrofusion dance-theatre production shaped by Esie Mensah’s lived experiences. Conceived over eight years, the work explores the courage needed to follow one’s calling and ancestral purpose. The piece follows a young woman discovering her power as she exists between worlds, guided by her Ancestors toward her chosen destiny. 
Esie Mensah is an award-winning choreographer, director, dancer, educator, and TEDx speaker whose work spans dance, theatre, opera, and film/TV. She has worked with Rihanna, Drake, Nelly Furtado, Kenny Ortega, and clients including Canada’s Got Talent, Holt Renfrew, Deloitte, and the Toronto Raptors. 
Her work has toured nationally and internationally. Theatre credits include choreography for Soulpepper, Obsidian, Shaw Festival, and Stratford Festival, as well as directing Serving Elizabeth at Theatre Aquarius. She choreographed Scott Joplin’s opera Treemonisha: A Musical Reimagining and was an Artist in Residence at Fall for Dance North in October 2025. 
Co-presented by Union and Fall for Dance North.

title: How Canadians are Feeling about Democracy These Days
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Trust in democratic institutions is being challenged in Canada and around the world. While many Canadians still believe in democratic values, more people are worried about political divisions, lower trust in governments and public institutions, false information, and whether political systems are meeting people's needs.
Using the latest public opinion polls, election research, and public engagement data, this panel will explore how Canadians feel about democracy today. Are concerns about democracy shared by many Canadians, or are they more common in certain groups? What is causing changes in political trust and participation? And what can governments, community organizations, educators, and local communities do to help strengthen democracy and encourage people to get involved in the future?
Featuring
Andrew Parkin
, Executive Director,
Environics Institute
Sarah Morra,
Chair, Vote 16 Canada and Research Assistant,
The Samara Centre for Democracy
Joanna Massie,
Postdoctoral Fellow in Political Science,
McMaster University
Moderator:
Shawn Micallef
, Toronto Star columnist & University of Toronto civics instructor
Toronto's municipal election takes place on October 26, 2026. Check out the
KnowYourVote.TO
website and the
Celebrate Democracy
page to learn more about the upcoming election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.
This initiative is made possible by donations to the Toronto Public Library Foundation and is generously supported by the McConnell Foundation.

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 1
location: North York Central Library, Room 1 (2nd floor)
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology. On November 4th, 2026, it will be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the moment of its discovery. Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will recount the story leading to the discovery of the tomb and explore the remarkable objects found in its first two chambers during the initial excavation in 1922.
Sherine ElSebaie is an Egyptologist who began her academic journey with a B.Sc. in Egypt, completed a Master’s degree in Egyptology at the University of Toronto. She then engaged in advanced doctoral studies, further deepening her expertise in the field. She specializes in ancient Egyptian art and religion, with particular interests in the history of archeology, tourism, and cultural heritage.
Registration is encouraged but not required.

by Michelle Zauner
Summary: Zauner, of indie band Japanese Breakfast, presents a memoir about growing up Korean-American, losing her mother, and forging her own identity. She tells of growing up the only Asian-American kid at her school in Eugene, Oregon; of struggling with her mother's high expectations of her; of a painful adolescence; of treasured months spent in her grandmother's tiny apartment in Seoul, where she and her mother would bond over heaping plates of food. As she grew up, her Koreanness began to feel ever more distant, even as she found the life she wanted to live. Her mother's diagnosis of terminal pancreatic cancer when Michelle was twenty-five forced a reckoning with her identity and brought her to reclaim the gifts of taste, language, and history her mother had given her.

title: Oct 15 - AI, ML, and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Place and Location**

Oct 15, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-october-15-2026)**

**Testing AI Systems in Production: Data Quality, Drift, and Model Evaluation**

AI systems can pass offline evaluation and still fail in production when real-world data changes, features become stale, labels or feedback signals are incomplete, or model behavior drifts away from expected outcomes. This talk shares practical patterns for testing and evaluating AI systems after deployment, including data quality checks, drift detection, online/offline metric comparison, model monitoring, and rollback analysis.

Using personalization and recommendation systems as examples, we will examine how teams can build evaluation workflows that catch quality issues before users do. Attendees will leave with a practical checklist for making AI-backed systems easier to evaluate, debug, and operate as data changes over time.

*About the Speaker*

[Jayakumar Ramalingam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jayakumarramalingam) is a Staff Software Engineer and Cloud Architect at SiriusXM with over 16 years of experience building cloud-native platforms, real-time data pipelines, resilient APIs, and AI/ML-enabled applications at production scale.

**Where Should Your Model Live? A Framework for Tiering Computer Vision Deployments**

Where should a computer vision model actually run - on-device, near the edge, or in the cloud? It's a decision that looks simple until requirements like latency, cost, connectivity, and update cadence start pulling in different directions, often revealing themselves only after deployment.

Drawing on hands-on experience developing and deploying CV models across Hailo, Nvidia, Qualcomm and AWS platforms, this talk introduces a practical framework for tiering computer vision deployments based on real project requirements and constraints. Discussion will include what changes at each tier - from development to deployment to monitoring and update strategy - with relevant industry examples.

Attendees will leave with a set of questions or a framework they can use to place their own CV projects into the right tier.

*About the Speaker*

[Ajaykumaar Sivacoumare](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ajay-sa/) is an AI Software Engineer specializing in computer vision and edge AI, with production experience developing and deploying CV models across Nvidia, Hailo, Qualcomm and AWS-based platforms.

**From 2D Slices to 3D Tumors: Lightweight Volumetric Detection Without Heavy 3D Networks**

Slice-wise 2D detectors are fast and scalable, but they struggle to produce reliable 3D bounding boxes from volumetric medical data. This talk presents YOLO-PVC, a lightweight post-processing framework that consolidates slice-wise YOLO detections into coherent 3D bounding boxes using percentile-based geometric aggregation and a minimal MLP calibration module.

This talk demonstrates consistent improvements in volumetric IoU across three liver tumor categories i.e., HCC, CCA, and Mixed, without requiring dense 3D annotations or memory-intensive architectures. The talk covers the clinical motivation, the technical approach, and practical lessons from deploying computer vision on real hospital MRI data.

*About the Speaker*

[Talha Waqas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mtalha-waqas-255557144/) is a second-year PhD student at ESME Research Lab, Paris and LISSI, Université Paris-Est, working on computer vision applied to medical imaging, with a focus on tumor classification, detection, and segmentation in multi-phase liver MRI.

**The Two-Loop Architecture for Voice AI**

Building responsive voice AI requires balancing latency with intelligence. This talk introduces a practical architecture that separates real-time conversation from asynchronous reasoning, enabling richer interactions without slowing the user experience. The session covers reusable design patterns drawn from production-inspired conversational AI systems.

*About the Speaker*

[Abhinav Tushar](https://lepisma.xyz/wiki/about/) is an ML engineer and researcher specializing in Conversational AI and Speech Technology.

description:

About Aggie Armstrong
Aggie Armstrong is a Filipino-Canadian artist living and working in Ontario. Working primarily in painting while incorporating hand embroidery and textile elements, she creates layered work inspired by everyday experiences, personal history, and the ways we make sense of the world around us.
 
Her work has been exhibited across Canada, the United States, and France, and she has exhibited at The Artist Project in Toronto since 2022. In 2023, she was commissioned to create the official poster for the Royal Agricultural Winter Fair, and in 2022 she was an artist-in-residence at Château Orquevaux in France. Her work has also been featured in British Vogue, Art Seen Magazine, CTV News, CP24 Breakfast, the Create!, and Colour Me Happy podcasts.
 
Alongside her studio practice, Aggie teaches watercolour workshops throughout the GTA and Southwestern Ontario, creating welcoming, approachable experiences that help people build confidence and discover the joy of painting and creativity.

title: History of Philosophy Research Group Talk (Bridger Ehli, IU-Bloomington)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The History of Modern Philosophy Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Bridger Ehli, an assistant professor in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Indiana – Bloomington. His research concerns themes in epistemology, metaphysics, and the philosophy of mind in early modern European philosophy. He is especially interested in early modern discussions of skepticism, especially as they relate to questions about mental representation, concepts, and the psychology of belief. Most of his work has focused on Hume’s contributions to these issues. In a forthcoming book, he argues that much of Hume’s skepticism arises from his thinking about the limits of intelligibility rather than those of justified belief. 
Title
Spinoza, the Cartesian Circle, and the Intelligibility of Doubt 
Abstract
Notoriously, Descartes’s epistemological procedure in the Meditations appears circular, presupposing the veracity of clear and distinct perception in order to establish that veracity. Although Spinoza does not himself face the Cartesian Circle, he discusses it in his Principles of Cartesian Philosophy and proposes an alternative to Descartes’s own response. I argue that Spinoza’s solution rests on an emendation of the mind’s conceptual capacities. He accepts that the hypothesis of a deceiving God undermines certainty concerning clear and distinct perception, but he denies that removing this reason for doubt requires coming to know that God exists and is not a deceiver. Instead, forming a clear and distinct idea of God renders the skeptical hypothesis unintelligible, so that it ceases to qualify as a genuine reason for doubt. This solution, modeled on the cogito’s immunity to doubt, retains the Cartesian commitment to the inconceivability of divine deception and does not require antecedent restriction on the scope of metaphysical doubt.

title: Open Studio: Esie Mensah’s ZAYO
location: West Wing, 65 Front Street West, Toronto, ON, M5R 1V9, Canada
description:
With Open Studio, Union and Fall for Dance North invite you into the daily life of a dancer. If you’re passing through Union Station’s West Wing, pause for a moment or stay for an hour and experience the artists at work. 
From 4–7 PM, experience Toronto-based dancer and choreographer Esie Mensah in process as she rehearses ZAYO with her company of dancers. 
ZAYO is an Afrofusion dance-theatre production shaped by Esie Mensah’s lived experiences. Conceived over eight years, the work explores the courage needed to follow one’s calling and ancestral purpose. The piece follows a young woman discovering her power as she exists between worlds, guided by her Ancestors toward her chosen destiny. 
Esie Mensah is an award-winning choreographer, director, dancer, educator, and TEDx speaker whose work spans dance, theatre, opera, and film/TV. She has worked with Rihanna, Drake, Nelly Furtado, Kenny Ortega, and clients including Canada’s Got Talent, Holt Renfrew, Deloitte, and the Toronto Raptors. 
Her work has toured nationally and internationally. Theatre credits include choreography for Soulpepper, Obsidian, Shaw Festival, and Stratford Festival, as well as directing Serving Elizabeth at Theatre Aquarius. She choreographed Scott Joplin’s opera Treemonisha: A Musical Reimagining and was an Artist in Residence at Fall for Dance North in October 2025. 
Co-presented by Union and Fall for Dance North.

title: How Do AIs "Think"? And Why They Get Things Wrong
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning.
In this class, we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. Develop an intuitive understanding of how AIs "think" without the math. We'll talk about how AIs remember, how they don't and how they are both similar and different to humans. And we'll ask the question underneath it all: is there anyone home inside the machine?
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: San Francisco: An evening with U of T Professor Jacob Tsimerman, Fields Medal winner
location: CANOPY Jackson Square
description:
Join us for a special evening featuring Professor Jacob Tsimerman (HBSc 2006), one of Canada’s leading mathematicians and a 2026 Fields Medal recipient.  
Recognized for resolving the Griffiths conjecture, recently appointed scientific director of the new Mathematics and AI Safety Institute in the Bay Area, and set to join OpenAI’s safety division, Professor Tsimerman will explore the evolving landscape of AI and safety, and the opportunities and challenges shaping our future.  
A networking reception will immediately follow with Chris Yip, Dean of the Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering and Stephen Wright, Dean of the Faculty of Arts & Science.   
Open to all U of T alumni and friends.  
Register 
About the speaker
 
Professor Jacob Tsimerman
Jacob Tsimerman is a Canadian mathematician and a professor in the Department of Mathematics in the Faculty of Arts & Science at the University of Toronto. His research focuses on analytic number theory and arithmetic geometry, particularly the study of integer solutions to certain types of polynomial equations.  
Born in Russia, Tsimerman developed an interest in mathematical puzzles at the age of three. He won two gold medals as a high school student at the International Mathematical Olympiad, including a perfect score in 2004. He studied mathematics at the University of Toronto as an undergraduate student and received his PhD from Princeton University in 2011, under the supervision of Peter Sarnak.  
Tsimerman held a postdoctoral position at Harvard University as a Junior Fellow of the Harvard Society of Fellows. In July 2014, he was awarded a Sloan Research Fellowship from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation and began his term as assistant professor at the University of Toronto, where he currently holds the position of full professor.  
Tsimerman is widely recognized for his contribution to proving the long-standing André-Oort conjecture in 2021, a milestone in modern mathematics that links special points with broader geometric structures, which has since unlocked new avenues of research inquiry. This included establishing key results in functional transcendence theory, most notably, the Ax-Schanuel theorem for Hodge structures. He is also recognized for resolving the Griffiths conjecture, developing an o-minimal version of the GAGA theorems. He was awarded a 2026 Fields Medal from the International Mathematical Union in recognition of these and other achievements.  
Tsimerman was the Distinguished Visiting Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study’s  School of Mathematics for its 2025-26 Special Year on Arithmetic Geometry, Hodge Theory, and o-minimality.  
He was elected a fellow of both the Royal Society and the Royal Society of Canada in 2025, and was awarded the 2024 John L. Synge Award, the 2023 Ostrowski Prize, the 2022 New Horizons in Mathematics Prize, the 2019 Coxeter-James Prize and the 2015 Sastra Ramanujan Prize.

title: Looking at Picture Books
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Marina Nemat: Mistress of the Persian Boarding House
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents internationally bestselling author Marina Nemat in conversation with Farah Heron at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In her debut work of historical fiction, Mistress of the Persian Boarding House, Nemat turns to the extraordinary life of her paternal grandmother, Zina, a Russian woman who fled the chaos of the 1917 Revolution and rebuilt her life in Iran. There, in a boarding house that becomes a refuge for other displaced women, Zina forms an unbreakable bond with fellow outsiders from Russia and Iran, women who support one another through childbirth, illness, poverty, political upheaval, and a pandemic. Amid this turmoil, Zina's path crosses with the ambitious Reza Khan, the future Shah of Iran, whose presence in her life becomes both an escape and a source of enduring hardship and sorrow.
Spanning decades and alternating between Zina's years in Russia and her later life in Iran, this sweeping novel asks: what does it mean to build a home and a family from nothing, in the wreckage of empire and revolution?
Drawing on her own family history and her lifelong engagement with themes of exile, resilience, and the search for home, first explored in her internationally bestselling memoir Prisoner of Tehran, Nemat brings the same unflinching honesty and tenderness to her grandmother's story that made her own so unforgettable.
Join Marina Nemat for an intimate conversation about inheritance, chosen family, and the quiet heroism of women who have had to build their lives twice.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: OTTAWA:  Culture in the Capital (9th trip)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
Can you join us in **Ottawa**?

*For a cultural long weekend! **Our 9th Ottawa trip!***

This trip is in just 3 months. Cooler days!

Dates/details are now FIRM--early FALL. **After Thanksgiving.**

PLEASE read everything over before signing up--all the details are here.

We will continue to explore the culture scene in some of our favorite Cities. **A deep dive/below the surface.**

Each year we bounce back and forth between Montreal & Ottawa.

This year in Ottawa--we'll also spend some time again in **GATINEAU** (Hull) for the second time--we can ***WALK*** between downtown Ottawa and downtown Hull (it takes just 30 minutes!!)

This will be our 9th 'long weekend' Ottawa trip since 2015. (--not the sleepy city you think it is--)

**Very important, PLEASE read all the information over before you RSVP.**
**You must contact me first. There is a *Non-Refundable fee* to join us.**

**Emailed/payable when you are confirmed.**

**$100 per person**

**Our 2026 (FALL) Ottawa trip will be built around**--our favorite contemporary galleries, architecture, public art, The National Gallery, Canadian Museum of History+++ food/drink. National Arts Centre.

**Plus our other usual favorite stops,** and a Group dinner.

All in 2 1/2 days!!

We are on the go each day from 10:30am-9pm, and **walk** everywhere.

Ottawa is the least expensive of our trips--perhaps $1000 all in?

What else do we do? Some combo of:

-visit other private/public galleries
-architecture tour/talks/walks
-Indigenous exploration
-public outdoor art
-food/drink
-other things which we don't yet know about
-much of what we do is FREE

**Note:** there is so much going on in Ottawa with regards to ART and CULTURE--don't think otherwise! We are welcomed everywhere.

This is a 3-night trip. The dates of this trip are AFTER Thanksgiving weekend.

**How these trips work:**

**YOU look after** your travel and accommodations (everyone has own personal budgets), **I look after** everything else. I plan ALL our activities on the ground while we are together. From first night drink/gallery visit (Thursday), to last night's group dinner (Saturday). You leave as you like on Sunday.

1. 3 nights (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) We meet as a group on Thursday at 5pm SHARP.
2. VIA train is currently showing $150 round trip ticket. How will you get there, where will you stay? Drive, bus, train, fly? (Your Presto card works in Ottawa--on public transit!)
3. Will you drive your car? Use 'points' for accommodations? Airbnb, B&B, Hotel, other? Do you need any insurance? You should aim to stay within a 15 mins walk of downtown/Byward Market. We walk everywhere!
4. There is a **NON-refundable fee sent to me when you signup/RSVP--due within 2 days.** I organize everything on the ground, discounts, tours, reservations etc. **TRIP FEE for 2026 is $100 per person.**
5. We will start with 10 people..until we know more about group sizing. But no more than 12 people.
6. Build into your trip budget: $75 for tickets/tours/entry, and $125 for our famous last night **group dinner**--we always find someplace special/memorable. Excellent OTTAWA food scene.
7. And of course, with all our trips there are always special/vip type surprises.
8. Agenda/schedule/Details in due course. You want to be in Ottawa and able to MEET up by **5pm on Thursday October 15th**. At the National Gallery.

Please read everything over before signing up. I keep you in the loop as per our planning, with a final schedule sent to you a few weeks before.

title: Flashback (X Avant XXI: Memory Mannnnn, Night 2)
location: First Unitarian Church,473 Oakwood Ave, York, ON M6C 2R5, Canada
description:
Sonic Bikes improvises with the soundworld of bicycles, and Bilal Nasser’s a punk & post-rock infused set delves into resistance, commemoration, and lament.

In the first set, local artist Stephanie Orlando brings her Sonic Bikes to the stage. A bespoke ensemble of improvising percussionists will make use of reassembled and sonified bike parts to animate a familiar soundworld of gears, spokes, and pedals. The performance takes on added weight as each artist exerts and sustains a particular pedal-powered labour to realize the piece, which is found in their constantly negotiated collective space.

During each of the other nights of the festival, Stephanie’s sound sculptures will be set up in the venue for audiences to interact and improvise with.

During the second set, Bilal Nasser will perform delay- and reverb-drenched solo works for guitar and voice. He will also be joined by a chamber ensemble to present a genre-bending suite about genocidal crisis and diasporic despair. Bilal blends post-rock, post-classical, punk, electronic, and shoegaze in a musical statement of commemoration, resistance, healing and lament. This performance marks the Toronto launch of Bilal’s album, Every Martyr is a Universe, on Constellation Records.

All prices are inclusive of HST.

title: 2026 Annual Toronto Graduate Philosophy Conference
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 100 (Main Floor Lecture Hall), 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
Join us for the 25th Annual Toronto Graduate Philosophy Conference with keynote speakers Don Garrett (NYU) and Alva Noë (University of California, Berkeley). 
Don J. Garrett is Silver Professor of Philosophy at New York University. He specializes in early modern philosophy, with particular interests in the philosophy of David Hume, Baruch Spinoza, and Mary Shepherd, and in areas including epistemology, metaphysics, philosophy of mind, and ethics. He is the author of Cognition and Commitment in Hume’s Philosophy (1997), Hume (2015), and Nature and Necessity in Spinoza’s Philosophy (2018), and editor of The Cambridge Companion to Spinoza (1996), and has also published numerous articles on early modern philosophy and related topics in leading academic journals. 
Alva Noë is Professor of Philosophy and Chair of the Department of Philosophy at the University of California, Berkeley. His research focuses on consciousness, perception, the philosophy of mind, and the philosophy of art. He is the author of Action in Perception (2004), Out of Our Heads: Why You Are Not Your Brain and Other Lessons from the Biology of Consciousness (2009), Strange Tools: Art and Human Nature (2015), and The Entanglement: How Art and Philosophy Make Us What We Are (2023), among other books. He has published extensively in academic journals and also writes for a broader public, with essays appearing in venues including The New York Times and The Atlantic.

title: The Annual Dante Lecture 'Between Ulysses and Saint Francis: Models of Leadership in Dante'
location: Alumni Hall 400
description:
Please join us on October 16th, 2026 for our Day of Dante! 



Marking the 800th anniversary of the death of Saint Francis, this year’s lecture – Between Ulysses and Saint Francis: Models of Leadership in Dante – traces how Dante’s Divine Comedy offers a powerful vision of charismatic leadership through the contrasting figures of Ulysses and Saint Francis of Assisi. This year’s Dante Lecture will be presented by Heather Webb, Professor of Italian Studies at Yale University. 



2026 Dante celebrations will begin with The Dante Garden Tour from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m., followed by the annual Dante Lecture from 6 to 7:30 p.m. and a Reception from 7:30 to 9 p.m. at the John M. Kelly Library featuring a new exhibit of the collection: Dante Sings the Praises of St. Francis. 



The Annual Dante Lecture is a cornerstone event celebrating the enduring importance of Dante’s work within literature, theology, philosophy, and cultural history. The lecture was established through the generosity of Alberto and Caroline Di Giovanni.

location: First Unitarian Church,473 Oakwood Ave, York, ON M6C 2R5, Canada
description:
Gathering two artist’s projects in concert form, Ancient Circuitry combines Mani Mazinani’s Solar Organ and Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong’s For The Youth: Reilluminated, connecting with ancestral knowledge today.

Solar Organ Ensemble moves between improvised and composed music using traditional and invented pentatonic scales covering a spectrum of approaches to pentatonic sound generation. Solar Organ https://manimazinani.net/project.html?project=Solar-Organ , an electronic pentatonic instrument created by Mani Mazinani, connects neurobiology with the geographic and historic ubiquity of pentatonic practice, a universal human phenomenon.

For The Youth: Reilluminated by Alexis Nanibush-Pamajewong, is a re-creation of a light and sound installation https://www.instagram.com/alexisnanibush_pamaj/p/DQngD8REaYa/?img_index=2 with local Indigenous youth performances — to honour the life, kinship, and the spirit of generations past, present, and future.

Curated by Mani Mazinani

INSTALLATION
Outside of performances, attendees can interact with sound sculptures from Night 2 https://musicgallery.org/events/flashback/ artist Stephanie Orlando.

Inspired by everyday sounds from her time working as a bike mechanic, Stephanie Orlando’s Sonic Bikes installation invites attendees to interact with the spectrum of noises and musical textures of recycled bike parts.

All prices are inclusive of HST.

title: Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam (The Seven Stages of Love) returns with a renewed artistic vision, bringing together poetry, music, dance, and storytelling to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: what does it mean to love?

Written and directed by Nishar Mansuri, the production is inspired by the Sufi understanding of ishq as a path of transformation. Through seven interconnected stages, the work moves from human longing to self-discovery, devotion, and surrender, inviting audiences into a journey that is both deeply personal and universal.

Featuring the poetry of Rumi, Amir Khusrau, Kabir, Bulleh Shah, Hafez, Fariduddin Attar, Sultan Bahu, and other mystic voices, the production reimagines centuries of mystical thought through contemporary performance. Their words become the foundation for an experience that transcends borders, languages, and faith traditions, inviting audiences to reflect on love as a force that connects us all.

title: Wilder Series: The Wilder Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**

**The loop is back and more wild than ever!**

For those unfamiliar, The Wilder Loop is 16 km of remote, rugged terrain through one of Ontario’s most untouched landscapes. Right from the start, the trail throws you into the wild: the first 5 km have everything we love about backcountry hiking; twisting forest paths, sweeping granite ridges, narrow boardwalks, and multiple beaver dams to scramble across. No two kilometers are the same, and every twist in the trail feels like a secret waiting to be found.

Once we hit the loop section, things get much quieter. This part of the park sees very few visitors as human footprints give way to moose tracks, and the rustling in the brush might just be one of the many beavers that call this area home.

Though the total elevation gain is relatively modest (about 260 m over the whole route), the trail’s difficulty comes from its remoteness, terrain, and ever-changing conditions. That said, for those willing to take it on, the reward is huge: sweeping views, total solitude, an unfiltered experience of Ontario’s boreal beauty... and a well-earned sense of pride by the time we make it back to the trailhead.

***Secret Location***
This is one of Wilderness Union's 'secret' hikes. As a group, we visit some truly special spots that are undiscovered by the wider world. We like to keep them pristine and only share them among our members- we ask that you do the same! We reveal the location to registered members in the days before the trip.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Untouched Wilderness:** Step into a landscape that feels frozen in time; wild, windswept, and wonderfully remote. Just you, the forest, and the sound of your boots on the trail.
**Wildlife Spotting:** Bears, moose, beavers and loons are just some of the creatures that call this area home. You'll have a chance to spot some from a safe distance for a magical encounter.
**Beaver Dam Crossings:** The area we're visiting is shaped by beavers. Tiptoe across nature’s original bridges- muddy, meticulously built, and surprisingly sturdy

**Event cost: $60+HST. $50 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/wilder-loop-fall-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: SOLD OUT: Birding with Beni: Fall Birding
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fall birding nature walk!
Fall migration is well underway! Join TBG Horticulturist and avid birder Sasan Beni for an engaging walk through the gardens and Wilket Creek Ravine, as you seek out the wildlife that call this place home. Learn how to identify the many different species passing through and how you can help them in their journey.
 
Bring your binoculars for a better view (we will have extras on hand) and a mug/thermos for a warm beverage and post-birding chat.
 
As with any wildlife tour, the spotting of birds and other wildlife is not guaranteed and is not within the control of the tour guide. Please be patient and considerate. The tour will not be rescheduled due to a lack of bird sightings. The tour will only be rescheduled due to inclement weather.
 
Meet at the TBG main entrance, just outside the George and Kathy Dembroski Centre for Horticulture.
 
Saturday, October 17, 8 to 10 a.m.
Public $22, Members $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Sasan Beni
Sasan Beni is a writer turned horticulturist. He graduated with a diploma in Environmental Landscape Management from Seneca College in King City, worked for the Toronto Zoo as a seasonal gardener, and joined TBG in 2020 as a seasonal Horticulturalist. His home is a revolving door of tropical plants. Beni is also passionate about birdwatching and wildlife photography. In the last three years, he has led many guided birdwatching walks around Toronto and has written several articles for Trellis magazine illustrated with his nature photographs.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Accessibility

description: Dates : Saturday and Sunday October 17-18 & 24-25 2026 Times : 10:00am - 4:00pm Location : 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Instructor : Janet Macpherson Unlock new creative possibilities in ceramics with our comprehensive Mold-Making 101 course. This hands-on class will guide you through the process of designing and creating plaster molds for both slip casting and press molding techniques. You’ll learn how to craft one-part and two-part molds, make decorative sprig molds, and combine slip-cast pieces into finished ceramic forms. This course is best for those with some hand-building experience. Throughout the course, you'll explore: - The fundamentals of plaster and its use in mold-making. - Techniques for creating and using press molds and sprig molds. - How to design and construct two-part molds for more complex shapes. - The basics of slip casting and assembling multi-part pieces. - Finishing techniques to prepare your work for firing and glazing. What you'll take home: - Your Molds of course! - 1 - 3 Slip cast pieces of each mold you complete Please note: 1) Glazing is not part of this course. You can book a glazing session seperately ($50) by emailing the technician at our Dupont Location. Glazing sessions include the use of our studio glazes. Firing fee is included. 2) Due to the hands-on and cumulative nature of this course, it's important to attend each session as we may not be able to repeat material covered in a missed class in a thorough way although we will try to catch you up. 3) By the end of the course, you'll have developed a new set of skills, a collection of unique molds, and the confidence to continue exploring mold-making in your own creative practice. title: Hurricane Hazel 2026 (SPECIAL ANNIVERSARY EDITION)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

On October 15, 1954, Toronto was devastated by the deadliest Hurricane of the 1954 season. Hazel was the most intense hurricane to hit the continent of North America in 1954.

Prior to the disaster that struck Toronto, the storm killed 469 people in Haiti, and the Caribbean before striking the United States. It roared ashore as a Category 4 hurricane.

After causing 95 deaths in the US, Hazel struck Ontario, raising the death toll by 81, mostly in Toronto. As a result of the high death toll and the damage caused, its name was retired from use.

But Toronto gained so much from the 1954 disaster, and our ravines and parklands are our lungs of the city. Thanks to Hazel we have our green spaces for generations to come.

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers with a few small hills and some steps. The tour begins outside the Weston Branch of the Toronto Public Library at Weston Road and 2 King Street, and returns to the starting location at the end of the walk. TTC bus routes are adjacent.

This special yearly tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

title: Wildlife-friendly Fall Gardens
location: Toronto Reference Library, Room B1 (located in the basement)
description:
At this time of year, many people admire the fall colours but also feel the need to rake and dispose of leaves, cut dead stems, and remove fallen branches. But what if this tidying up negatively affects our gardens and pollinators? While we may not see the bees and butterflies during the fall and winter, they are still around!
In this presentation, Dorte Windmuller, a Butterflyway Ranger of the David Suzuki Foundation, will discuss how to maintain and protect wildlife habitat even throughout the colder months, and how “leave the leaves” can help nature come back stronger the next season.

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

title: Meet New People, Great Conversations & 50+ Board Games | 25–45 | Fast Friends
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Ever wish there were an easier way to turn a room full of strangers into people you actually want to talk to?
*That’s what Fast Friends is designed for.*

Instead of arriving at a busy pub and wondering who to approach, our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, giving you the chance to meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You get a little structure to make connecting easier — without making the evening feel forced or formal.

And once the hosted rounds finish, you can keep the evening going. 🎲
We’re back at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown — a relaxed Irish pub with food, drinks and 50+ board games, giving you plenty of ways to continue socialising with the people you’ve met.

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto17thoct.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto17thoct.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10
Regular: CAD $15
At the Door: CAD $20 cash — to host Faye
Booking ahead helps us plan the right group size and venue space, and your ticket confirms your place.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Faye, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? Completely fine. Many guests arrive solo, and we’ll help you get comfortable and connected from the start.
7:30 PM — Fast Friends
This is where the evening gets going.
You’ll move through a series of short, guided conversations, meeting different people along the way. Our host keeps the rotations moving, so you don’t have to worry about who to approach or what to do next.
Just show up, join the conversation and see who you click with.

✨ Themed Connection Rounds
Throughout the evening, we’ll mix in themed rounds and interactive prompts designed to make connecting easier.
They’ll help you discover shared interests, experiences and unexpected things you have in common — taking the conversation beyond the usual small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — Board Games & Socialising
Once the hosted rounds finish, the evening doesn’t have to.
Stout has 50+ board games available, making it easy to keep the conversations going. Pick a game with the people you’ve met, grab another drink, join a group or simply continue chatting.
You don’t have to be a serious gamer — the games are simply another easy way to socialise and get to know people.

🍻 Staying Later?
Stout’s current After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 15–25 new people in one evening
✔️ Guided conversations make meeting people easier
✔️ Meet different people through rotating conversations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games available afterwards 🎲
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Most guests come solo
✔️ Plenty of time to keep socialising after the hosted rounds
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

👋 Who Is It For?
Ages 25–45
Whether you’ve just moved to Toronto, have lived here for years, or simply feel like your social circle could use some fresh faces, you’re welcome.
You don’t need to know anyone beforehand or arrive with a group.
Come by yourself, bring a friend, or simply come ready to have a few good conversations and see where the evening takes you.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come for the conversations. Stay for the games. Leave with new connections. ❤️

title: Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Ishq Ke Saat Muqaam (The Seven Stages of Love) returns with a renewed artistic vision, bringing together poetry, music, dance, and storytelling to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: what does it mean to love?

Written and directed by Nishar Mansuri, the production is inspired by the Sufi understanding of ishq as a path of transformation. Through seven interconnected stages, the work moves from human longing to self-discovery, devotion, and surrender, inviting audiences into a journey that is both deeply personal and universal.

Featuring the poetry of Rumi, Amir Khusrau, Kabir, Bulleh Shah, Hafez, Fariduddin Attar, Sultan Bahu, and other mystic voices, the production reimagines centuries of mystical thought through contemporary performance. Their words become the foundation for an experience that transcends borders, languages, and faith traditions, inviting audiences to reflect on love as a force that connects us all.

title: Cliffs & Fall Colours: A Bruce Peninsula Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**The Bruce Peninsula does dramatic better than almost anywhere else in Ontario, and fall is when it really shows off.**

We'll be out for most of the day, covering 8.5km of moderate hiking through some of the best autumn scenery in the province, with the changing leaves against the escarpment's limestone making for a proper contrast.

We'll start in the forest before the trail opens onto the coastline, tracing the cliffs down to the Grotto. It's the most photographed spot on the peninsula for good reason: crystal clear water, a sea cave carved into the rock, and a natural window out to the bay. We'll take our time here, including a stop for lunch.

From the Grotto we'll keep following the shoreline out to Stormhaven, crossing pebble beaches with open views across Georgian Bay the whole way. We'll turn around there and retrace the coastline back, catching all the same cliffs and colour from the other direction with the light shifted by then.

**Two important things to note:**

1. **Self driving isn't possible for this trip. Parking passes at the trailhead sell out well in advance, so all members travel together on WU transport.**
2. **Bruce Peninsula National Park is stunning, but be aware that it is a long drive there and back. Full details are in the itinerary below.**

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**The Grotto:** The peninsula's most famous natural feature: a limestone sea cave with turquoise water and a rock window looking out over Georgian Bay.
**Stormhaven Coastline:** A stretch of cobble beach with wide open views across the bay, well past where most day hikers turn around.
**Fall Colour on the Escarpment:** Peak autumn colour against the Niagara Escarpment's pale limestone cliffs, a contrast you don't get anywhere else on the Bruce Trail\*\*.\*\*

**Event cost: $140+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/bruce-peninsula-26)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Paper Quilling: Fall Tree Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Celebrate the magic of autumn with a relaxing day of creativity at the beautiful Toronto Botanical Garden!
Join artist Deepa Krishnan for a fun, beginner-friendly paper quilling workshop. In this 4-hour session, you’ll learn a variety of quilling techniques while creating a stunning fall tree on an 8”x10” canvas. Inspired by the rich colours of the season, you’ll have the freedom to choose your own autumn palette, making your artwork truly one of a kind.
 
This workshop includes a 30-minute lunch break. We recommend bringing your own lunch to enjoy while taking in the beautiful surroundings of the garden.
 
Whether you’re trying paper quilling for the first time or looking to expand your skills, this workshop is a wonderful way to slow down, get creative, and celebrate the beauty of the season.
 
All supplies are included, and no prior experience needed. This workshop is suitable for adults and children ages 12 and above.
 
Sunday, October 18, 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Public $100, TBG Members $90 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level, and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

title: Impressionist Afternoon Tea + 3 Exhibits at the AGO
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Sunday, October 18th**, join me for an **Impressionist Afternoon Tea in the Norma Ridley Members’ Lounge to celebrate the connection between art, atmosphere and indulgence.** Inspired by the luminous colours and expressive brushstrokes of *[Impressionist Revolution: Monet to Matisse from the Dallas Museum of Art](https://ago.ca/exhibitions/impressionist-revolution-monet-matisse-dallas-museum-art)* we saw last month, this seasonal Afternoon Tea offers an elegant, leisurely escape into art, conversation and thoughtfully crafted flavours that reflect the beauty and softness of this exhibit. Delicate savoury selections and whimsical pastries are designed to evoke sunlit gardens, countryside picnics and the romance of Impressionism. Since Afternoon Tea includes free admission to the Gallery, we will see more Impressionism art that was not part of our August visit - **Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism**, **Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic**, and a new exhibit that will open the day before - **In Plain Sight: Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames**. **I** **have booked a table for Sunday October 18th at 2:30pm, and can add members to it.**

**COST**
Adult: $80 + taxes + gratuity = $104.80

Meetup Organizer Fee: $5

**SIGNING-UP**

* **RSVP Yes** **\- everyone goes on the waitlist until confirmed\.**
* **I will reach out to provide my email address for the etransfer of $109.80 and I will call in to add you to our table. Once I receive confirmation, I will inform you and move you to attending.**
* There are no refunds.

A reminder will be sent the day before with my cell and reminder details where to meet and when.

RSVPs close 3 days prior and the Waitlist will be removed at that time. Cancellations will result in a No Show and impact future attendance.

**MEETUP TIME**
**Meet me at: 1:45pm inside the entrance to the right side of the AGO at 317 Dundas St. W. We will then scan our tickets and head over to the exhibits, prior to Tea.**

**Note: We must enter the AGO together for our tea reservation.**

**EXHIBITS**
**Reality & Reverie: Canadian and European Painting Beyond Impressionism** (Level 1 Gallery 127)

**Steam: Impressionist Painting Across the Atlantic** (Level 1 Gallery 116)

**Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Picture Frames** (Level 1 Gallery 115)

**Meet me for Afternoon Tea: at 2:30pm in front of the** **Norma Ridley Members’ Lounge (Level 1)** (Please do not go to our table before I get there)

Enjoy and please post your comments in the Event after.

title: Beginner Crochet - October
location: Bistitchual, 266 Jane St, Toronto, ON M6S 3Z2
description: This listing is for a two session Beginner Crochet Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday October 18th and 25th from 2:30pm-4:00pm Learn the fundamentals of crochet in this two part class. We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! Cancellation Policy Classes must be paid for at the time of registration to reserve your spot. - If cancelled 48 hrs or more prior to the start of the first class will be given a store credit. Classes cancelled less than 48 hrs prior to the start of the class will not be reimbursed.

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: A Good War
location: Toronto Reference Library, Lower Level, Room B1
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
October’s book is
A Good War: Mobilizing Canada for the Climate Emergency
by public policy advisor Seth Klein. Copies of the book are available in print, eBook & eAudiobook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In A Good War, Seth Klein explores how we can align our politics and economy with what the science says we must do to address the climate crisis. But Klein brings an original and uniquely hopeful take to this challenge. The book is structured around lessons from the Second World War – the last time Canada faced an existential threat. Others have said we need a “wartime approach” to climate change, but this is the first book to delve into what that could actually look like. Canada’s wartime experience, Klein contends, provides an inspirational reminder that
we have done this before
. We have mobilized in common cause across class, race and gender, and entirely retooled our economy in the space of a few short years."
Drop in. No registration required.

“The truth is that we are one body moving through time together.” — Richard Wagamese 
How do we love and care for ourselves, one another, and our world? 
Embedded in the depth of our being we hold the truth of all creation. Clay grounds us and reconnects us to our shared humanity, the fertile Earth, and all life. Guided by a Zen practitioner and registered art therapist, engage in the simple physical practice of breath with clay.

title: The Information Battle: Elections, Journalism and Misinformation
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall
description:
As elections take place in an increasingly complicated online world, voters are exposed to a huge mix of news, social media posts, AI-generated content, and false information spread by organized groups. New digital technologies have made it easier for people to learn about issues and take part in civic life, but they have also raised concerns about trust, fair elections, and respectful public discussion.
This panel brings together experts in misinformation, journalism, and election administration to explore the challenges and opportunities facing democracy today. How are AI and new technologies changing the way people get information? What do these changes mean for voters, journalists, and election officials? And what can be done to build public trust in elections while helping people stay informed and engaged in public life?
Featuring
Nick Hune-Brown
Journalist and Author
Award-winning magazine writer and Executive Editor at The Local
Valérie Kindarji
Political scientist
University of Toronto focused on the impacts of disinformation on democracies in Europe and North America and Lab Manager at the University of British Columbia.
Tobias Novogrodsky
Deputy City Clerk
Election Services, City of Toronto
Moderator by:
Anita Li
CEO and editor-in-chief of The Green Line
Toronto's municipal election takes place on October 26, 2026. Check out the
KnowYourVote.TO
website and the
Celebrate Democracy
page to learn more about the upcoming election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.

title: David Treuer: The Savage Mind
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
New York Times bestselling author David Treuer shares his groundbreaking, intimate reckoning with the history of North America.
The Savage Mind is a seamless blend of memoir, history and reportage, in which Treuer leverages his unique dual perspective as the son of a Holocaust survivor and the first American Indigenous woman judge in the United States to offer an examination of the distinct nature of North American violence.
In contrast to the frontier thesis of American history, Treuer contends that frontier violence cannot be defined as an external force, but that it has actually entered the culture and taken root in our very selves.
By reckoning with these histories, the book confronts our complicity in either normalizing violence, or blaming it on outside sources, instead of seeing its recurring patterns and contending with its significance.
David Treuer speaks with journalist and author Tanya Talaga about The Savage Mind and shares why he chooses to embrace an ultimately hopefully view of the continent.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

Acclaimed journalist and former deputy prime minister Chrystia Freeland joins Star business columnist Adam Radwanski for the launch of Toronto Star Live at Soulpepper — a conversation about what Canada and other democracies owe each other, and themselves, when the old rules no longer apply. How should Canada respond when powerful countries — including its closest neighbours — become unpredictable partners?

Her new book, Unreliable Boyfriend: An Insider’s View of Dealing with a Chaotic Superpower, Plutocrats and Other Complicated People, is a firsthand account of that pressure — and an argument for what comes next.

More information and tickets can be found here: https://soulpepper.ca/toronto-star-live-in-conversation-with-chrystia-freeland/ https://soulpepper.ca/toronto-star-live-in-conversation-with-chrystia-freeland/ .

Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

description:

Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact

title: Customer Segmentation: Who Will Pay for Your Product?
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground Floor
description:
This program is part of the Toronto Reference Library's
Entrepreneur in Residence
(EIR) service.
The fastest way to start a new business is to try to sell it to everybody. This session will teach you to narrow down your target group by using geography, demographics, and behavioral statistics to determine demand. It will also cover how to spot your early adopters, i.e., the people who need what you're building most will be flexible while you get it right. Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.
This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz.
By completing the specialization,
you will learn:
How AI works
How to write effective prompts
How to use generative AI tools responsibly
How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm
How to stay up to date with AI news
After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions.
No AI experience is required.
How to Joi
n a Learning Circle:

Please sign up with a
valid email address
.
A valid TPL library card is required for online circles.

title: ABCD Reads "Salvation of a Saint" by Keigo Higashino
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads "**[Salvation of a Saint](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C2888913)**" by Keigo Higashino.

[RESULTS of the poll for this event]

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"The Devotion of Suspect X was a hit with critics and readers alike. The first major English language publication from the most popular bestselling writer in Japan, it was acclaimed as "stunning," "brilliant," and "ingenious."
Now physics professor Manabu Yukawa—Detective Galileo—returns in a new case of impossible murder, where instincts clash with facts and theory with reality.
Yoshitaka, who was about to leave his marriage and his wife, is poisoned by arsenic-laced coffee and dies. His wife, Ayane, is the logical suspect—except that she was hundreds of miles away when he was murdered. The lead detective, Tokyo Police Detective Kusanagi, is immediately smitten with her and refuses to believe that she could have had anything to do with the crime. His assistant, Kaoru Utsumi, however, is convinced Ayane is guilty. While Utsumi's instincts tell her one thing, the facts of the case are another matter. So she does what her boss has done for years when stymied—she calls upon Professor Manabu Yukawa.
But even the brilliant mind of Dr. Yukawa has trouble with this one, and he must somehow find a way to solve an impossible murder and capture a very real, very deadly murderer.
Salvation of a Saint is Keigo Higashino at his mind-bending best, pitting emotion against fact in a beautifully plotted crime novel filled with twists and reverses that will astonish and surprise even the most attentive and jaded of readers." (from [Macmillan Publishers](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9781250036278/salvationofasaint/))

"When a man is discovered dead by poisoning in his empty home his beautiful wife, Ayane, immediately falls under suspicion. All clues point to Ayane being the logical suspect, but how could she have committed the crime when she was hundreds of miles away?
As Tokyo police detective Kusanagi tries to unpick a seemingly unrelated sequence of events he finds himself falling for Ayane. When his judgement becomes dangerously clouded his assistant must call on an old friend for help; it will take a genius to unravel the most spectacular web of deceit they have ever faced…
SALVATION OF A SAINT is a magnificently complex and page-turning thriller starring international crime fiction’s most enigmatic sleuth.This is essential reading for all fans of exceptional crime fiction." (from [Hachette UK](https://www.hachette.co.uk/titles/keigo-higashino/salvation-of-a-saint/9780349138817/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.
