title: Jamaluddin Aram: The Blood of Things
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents Afghan-Canadian writer Jamaluddin Aram in conversation with Dmitri Nasrallah at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
What does it mean to carry a homeland inside you after it has been lost, not once, but again and again? In his essay collection
The Blood of Things
, Aram turns his attention fully to Afghanistan, its beauty, its suffering, and its complexity. Spanning from the recent fall of Kabul to the early days of Islam, from the myth of the Order of Assassins to the persecution of the country's ethnic Hazara community, Aram weaves personal stories with sweeping historical and political inquiry.
Drawing on his own journey from Afghanistan to Toronto, and his work as associate producer of the Oscar-nominated film
Buzkashi Boys
, Aram brings a novelist's eye for character and an essayist's rigor to bear on questions of identity, belonging, and what remains possible even amid profound loss.
Join Jamaluddin Aram for an intimate evening of readings and conversation on exile, memory, and the enduring pull of home.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jamaluddin Aram
Dimitri Nasrallah

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

n a Learning Circle:

title: Embodied Garden: 8-Week Art Therapy Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee, for an eight-week closed art therapy group for adults!
Embodied Garden invites participants to slow down, connect with nature, and explore their inner world through creative expression. Each session includes a brief embodiment meditation, gentle check-in, nature-inspired art-making, and optional sharing.
 
Across the eight weeks, the garden becomes both a setting and a metaphor for exploring themes of grounding, growth, movement, boundaries, protection, change, community, and belonging. Each session introduces a distinct theme while contributing to an overarching exploration of embodiment, connection, and our relationship with the natural world.
 
As a closed group, participants are invited to attend all eight sessions. The continuity of the series offers opportunities to build trust, develop connections, and reflect more deeply as the sessions unfold.
 
The group is facilitated by Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee who creates gentle, creative spaces that support reflection, care, growth, and connection. Art therapy uses the creative process as a way to explore emotions, experiences, relationships, and self-awareness, with no emphasis on artistic skill or producing a finished artwork.
 
Wednesdays, October 21 through December 9, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. (eight sessions).
Public $160, TBG Members $120 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Résumé and Cover Letter for Industry
description:
About the facilitator 
 
Jessica Wurster, Career Exploration & Education, Graduate Career Educator  
Jessica (she/they) has been supporting students in their career journeys for over 15 years at universities in Quebec and Ontario. As Graduate Career Educator, Jess draws on their doctoral training in Communication Studies and professional experience to develop and deliver programming and resources targeted to professional and graduate students and recent alumni. She’s also a quilter, a frequenter of farmer’s markets in the east end and beyond, and a collector of cookbooks.    
Looking to tune up your résumé and cover letter for industry roles? Join us for a session with Career Exploration & Education to learn strategies, tips, and AI-assisted approaches to build and refresh your industry job application materials.  
We will discuss:  

Creating application materials targeted to industry roles  
How to analyze industry job descriptions so you can successfully tailor your résumé  
Strategies to create a more effective and captivating résumé including writing strong accomplishment statements and organizing résumé sections effectively 
How to use AI tools effectively and ethically to support résumé and cover letter development, including prompt-engineering techniques that help generate stronger content, identify skills alignment, and customize materials for specific roles 
Best practices for reviewing, refining, and personalizing AI-generated content to ensure authenticity and accuracy 

Bonus Activity: Participate in a résumé review for personalized feedback! You will need to bring a digital copy of your working résumé (it does not need to be finalized) and be ready to share it with your peers. You’ll also can practice AI prompting strategies to strengthen and tailor your application materials  
Register in Advance.

title: Working With Your Go To Emotional State
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Most of us have a
"go-to emotion."
It is the emotion that shows up automatically when we feel hurt or overwhelmed. That emotion can be
anger, anxiety, depression, guilt, shame, or even emotional numbness.
In this interactive presentation, we will explore how your go-to emotion developed, what purpose it serves, and offer techniques on how to respond from a more measured space.
Join Ann Schnurr, a Registered Psychotherapist with more than 25 years of experience, as she supports adults to understand their go-to emotion for greater emotional resilience, healthier relationships, and a deeper connection with self.
Registration is encouraged
via the library’s website.
Drop-ins welcome until capacity is reached.  For more information contact the Business Science & Technology desk at 416-395-5613

title: The Friendship Test: Engagement Activity
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
The Friendship Test
Bring your best friend, your partner, or your whole crew and put your friendship to the test, Newlywed Game–style. Answer questions about each other's habits, histories and hot takes to see who really knows who, and who's got some catching up to do. It's playful proof that even our closest bonds have more to discover, echoing Berkowitz's case that friendship takes real, ongoing work.
This interactive pre-show is followed by
Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
, which starts at 7pm in the Appel Salon.
You can register for that event
here
, but please note if you wish to attend the pre-event activities you need to register separately
on this page
.
***
This evening’s
theme explores
the challenge of
staying in dialogue and connection across our
difference
s
through Hannah Arendt’s friendships
.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the
featured event
. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for the workshop or try out one of the engagement activities available, including this event's Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
The Kitchen Table |
5:30 – 6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: Bridging Minds: Menopause, Metabolism and Heart Health: What Changes at Midlife
description:
What happens to your heart and metabolism as you move through menopause? As hormone levels change through the transition, so can the way your body manages cholesterol, blood sugar, fat and other factors that influence long-term heart health.
Join Dr. Iliana Lega for the next Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations webinar to understand these changes and what you can do to support your health. Building on last month’s conversation about menopause and brain health, this session broadens the picture to explore heart and metabolic health, practical strategies for prevention, and what current evidence tells us about the role of menopausal hormone therapy.
What to Expect
What changes during menopause:
Understand how the menopause transition can affect cardiovascular risk factors, metabolism, body composition and weight.
What you can do:
Explore practical lifestyle and preventive strategies to support heart and metabolic health during midlife.
The role of hormone therapy:
Learn what current evidence tells us about menopausal hormone therapy and cardiovascular and metabolic health.
About the Presenter
Dr. Iliana Lega is a staff endocrinologist at Women’s College Hospital, and a scientist at the Women’s College Hospital Research and Innovation Institute. Dr. Lega’s clinical interests lie in the area of diabetes, as well as reproductive endocrinology, including Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (POI), Turner syndrome, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), and Menopause.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:
https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/

This virtual Zoom event is free to join but registration is required. Once registered, you’ll receive an email with the Zoom link.
We can’t wait to see you there!

title: New Sounds, New Space Report Launch + Wavelength Documentary Premiere
location: St. Anne's Parish Hall,651 Dufferin St, Toronto, ON M6K 2B2, Canada
description:
Presented with Sonic Boom


October 21, 2026
Wavelength @ St. Anne’s

651 Dufferin St.

6PM

Free - RSVP at http://bit.ly/NSNSwl


You are invited to join Wavelength for an evening of original content! Local music lovers will enjoy this free presentation, panel, and screening plus a networking session soundtracked by DJ Uncle Chayne.


Be the first to view Wavelength: 25 Years of Music & Community, a short documentary written and directed by Ian Daffern (Idfactory) telling the story of Toronto’s unique artist-run concert series and non-profit organization. A who’s who of Canadian music, this project was scored and mixed by Justin Small (Do Make Say Think, BODY///GRAVE) and music supervised by Babs V. Westerholm (Cue Queens) and features interviews with Melissa Auf der Maur (Hole, Smashing Pumpkins), Emilie Hanskamp, pHoenix Pagliacci, Charles Spearin (Broken Social Scene, Do Make Say Think), and Wavelength’s Jonathan Bunce (AKA Jonny Dovercourt). Additional music by Burs, Luge, MOONBEAN, Orbital Ensemble, Paul Chin, Pony Da Look, Rich Aucoin, Sook-Yin Lee and more.


A follow up to 2023’s acclaimed Reimagining Music Venues Study, the launch of the “New Sounds, New Space” report explores different pathways for establishing community hubs for Toronto’s grassroots music community. With positive case studies on Hugh’s Room Live, It’s Ok* Studios, Small World Music and Primal Note Studios, the report shines light on Toronto’s post-COVID music venue landscape while pointing the way forward for imaginative new spaces. Funded by Canada Council for the Arts “Seed” grant!


Join in on the conversation that shapes Toronto’s music culture from the ground up.

title: Friendships and other Complexities ft. Roger Berkowitz
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
This evening’s theme explores the challenge of staying in dialogue and connection across our differences through Hannah Arendt’s friendships.
Make the most of your
Connect IRL
experience by coming before or staying after the featured event. Grab a drink or snack at the bar. Sign up for
The Friendship Test Workshop
(see registration below) or try out one of the engagement activities available, including tonight’s
Conversation Station: The Kitchen Table
, where you can take a moment or two to connect with a stranger to reflect on the rewards and challenges of friendship.
*****
Join us at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon
for
Friendships and other Complexities
with political theorist Roger Berkowitz in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia.
This one is about the harder kind of connection: staying in relationships with people you disagree with. We'll consider friendship not as a private comfort but as political work; the daily, unglamorous business of talking with people whose views unsettle us and whose reasoning we may never fully understand. Expect to be asked what you're willing to hold open, and to talk it through with people who won't necessarily see it your way.
What can Hannah Arendt's friendships — including with people whose politics she found troubling — teach us about sustaining democracy today? If our current political crisis is, at its root, a crisis of friendship, what has eroded our capacity to stay in dialogue across difference? And in an age of mass loneliness and ideological certainty, what would it mean to treat friendship, rather than consensus or moral purity, as the foundation of democratic life?
Berkowitz is founder and academic director of the Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities at Bard College. In A World We Share: Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in a Broken World, he rethinks politics through Arendt's own life — a Jewish woman who escaped Nazi Germany, lived as an exile in Paris and then New York, and became a bold critic of popular ideas after World War II. People who knew her said she had a special talent for making friends. Berkowitz argues that a politics built solely on being right becomes cruel, coercive and ultimately anti-political.
Come ready to disagree agreeably.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Roger Berkowitz
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read more:
World We Share : Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship in A Broken World
***
Sign up for The Friendship Test Workshop
|
5:30 - 6:30 pm
The Kitchen Table |
5:30–6:30 pm & 8:00 – 9:00 pm
Grab a seat and dig into the questions we rarely ask out loud: How has your definition of friendship changed? Can you stay close to someone you disagree with? What makes a friendship last? Inspired by Berkowitz's argument that friendship — not agreement — is the glue of a healthy society, this café is a space to reflect on your own circle with the strangers sitting next to you.
Connect IRL
is not your average series of events, workshops and activities, but a real chance to connect with other Torontonians in meaningful and sometimes unexpected ways. Through conversation stations meant to spark one-on-one conversations, or hands-on engagement activities and workshops before the featured event, participants can explore the value of connection and community.

title: In-Depth Intro to Woodworking Oct 22 [Thursdays - 6 week Intensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
Woodworking at TTLMakerspace

 
 Suitable for beginners, this woodworking course is designed to teach you all that you need to get started in woodworking by learning both traditional, and modern techniques.

 Students will learn valuable hands-on skills working on instructor-lead projects using both hand and power tools.

 Projects are chosen to provide skills development in a natural progression from familiarity with the unique characteristics of wood, to basic essential techniques, to some more advanced topics.

 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- A complete understanding of the nature and properties of wood 

- Proficiency with traditional woodworking techniques

- Comfort working with chisels, planes, saws

- Proficiency with wood milling techniques

- Comfort with safe operation of power tools

- Familiarity with power planing, joiner, drill press, router and table saw 

- Dressing and laminating wood 

- Experience following project plans 

- Familiarity with joinery 

- Wood finishing, various treatments 

 
  Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

 Certifications for all courses are valid for one year from the time that they are issued, and can be renewed at no cost with your active monthly membership within 3 months of their expiry. Certification renewal requires booking with an instructor, is conducted at the makerspace, and helps you keep your skills current. 

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards 
 
 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Oct 22 - Advances in AI at Virginia Tech
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from AI researchers at Virginia Tech!

**Date, Time and Location**

Oct 22, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
**[Online. Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/advances-in-ai-at-virginia-tech-october-22-2026)**

**Multi-Agent Communication: A framework, diagnostic and mechanistic perspective**

Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used for collaborative reasoning, debate, and consensus, yet their communication dynamics remain poorly understood. This talk presents a framework for studying multi-agent communication through diagnostic and mechanistic perspectives.

I will discuss CONSENSAGENT, which improves consensus by mitigating sycophancy, alongside our diagnostic work on communication patterns and failure modes in real-world multi-agent debates. I will then present ongoing work that moves toward a mechanistic understanding of how these interaction patterns arise internally, with the broader goal of making multi-agent systems more interpretable, reliable, and controllable.

*About the Speaker*

[Priya Pitre](https://www.linkedin.com/in/priya-p-a31360117/) I am an Ph.D student in the Computer Science Department at Virginia Tech (VT), co-advised by Dr. Xuan Wang and Dr. Naren Ramakrishnan.

**Exposing and Improving Fine-Grained Visual Grounding Abilities of Lightweight Multimodal LLMs**

Lightweight multimodal LLMs can localize whole objects effectively, yet often struggle when a query targets a small object part or fine-grained visual detail. This talk presents a reasoning-guided framework that teaches compact models to ground parts through an explicit coarse-to-fine process: first locating the parent object, then identifying the requested part.

A part-aware reinforcement-learning objective provides stage-wise rewards for object accuracy, part containment, and the consistency of the model’s self-critique. Using these techniques, a compact 4B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot part grounding while preserving its object-level performance.

These advances can be used to enable lightweight MLLMs to support detail-oriented tasks in biology and robotics.

*About the Speaker*

[Kazi Mehrab ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ksmehrab/)I a CS PhD candidate at Virginia Tech, where I currently focus on multimodal LLMs and computer vision tasks, including visual perception, reasoning and grounding.

**Understanding Visual Generative Models for Precise Control**

Despite remarkable progress in image and video generation, translating user intent into precise and consistent visual outputs remains a challenge. This talk explores how understanding the representations within generative models can enable finer control over what they create.

It connects semantic image editing with compositional generation, examining how visual concepts can be isolated, manipulated, and combined while preserving their identity and surrounding content. Building on these insights, structured visual inputs provide a way to express complex intent through subject references, poses, and spatial layouts.

The discussion then extends from images to video, where representations must evolve to preserve scene continuity while accommodating motion and change. Together, these directions establish a unified perspective on how visual representations can support controllable editing, composition, and coherent generation across space and time.

*About the Speaker*

[Yusuf Dalva](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yusuf-dalva/) is a Ph.D. candidate at Virginia Tech, advised by Pinar Yanardag and affiliated with the Sanghani Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics.

title: What is Artificial Intelligence

description:

Come join this beginner in person class to learn what AI is, how it learns and predicts outcomes, considerations when using GenAI applications, and how the Internet of Things (IOT) applies to AI.

Learn what is Artificial Intelligence and how it interacts in our day to day activities.
Gain an understanding of how Artificial Intelligence learns and predicts outcomes.
Learn the importance of how data is integral to how Artificial Intelligence systems are built.

title: CNC Milling for Builders - Oct 22  [Thursdays - 6 Week Comprehensive]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
CNC for Builders 

 
 

 
 In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will go from beginner to a practical working knowledge of CAD modelling and CNC machining with an automated milling machine, specifically for furniture, cabinetry, frames etc. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Starting with desktop versions of CNC machines, you’ll work your way through lessons up to the industrial Omni 1350 6’ x 8’ CNC milling machine. 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Schedule : 
 
 
 Six three-hour weekly classes, Thursdays 6pm to 9pm. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Outcomes : 
 
 
 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- 
 A complete understanding of the steps needed to go from concept to completed part 

- 
 Familiarity with the properties of a variety of hardwood materials 

- 
 Experience and comprehension of the most important principles of CAD modelling 

- 
 Selecting and programming the most commonly used tools 

- 
 Full understanding of the most common machining operations 

- 
 Experience creating tool paths with CAM software 

- 
 Setting up a CNC mill and performing operations 

- 
 Machine maintenance and Safety 

 
 
 Following this course, you’ll be certified to use desktop mills, and book time with the industrial mill at TTLMakerspace (with your membership). You will also be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing CNC knowledge on our Discord community. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Useful for: furniture, cabinets, flat-pack, desktops, boats, frames 
 
 

 
 
 Want to get notified next time classes are posted? 

 Join our mailing list!

title: Data Analytics Essentials Online Learning Circle
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet online every Thursday evening,
September 24 - December 10, 6-7:30 PM
(12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.

description:
From Ancient Americas to Ancestral Abiayala

                    Thursday October 22, 2026

The Diane Wolfe Lecture 
Speaker: Juliana Ramírez Herrera, Ph.D., Assistant Professor of Indigenous Art and Archaeology of the Ancestral Americas and of Colonial Latin American Art, University of California, Berkeley 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    Join Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera, curator of the Gardiner Museum’s Ancestral Abiayala Gallery—formerly Ancient Americas—for a conversation on repatriation, broadly understood, and how it shaped her vision for the renovated space. 
Drawing on other threads of her research, Dr. Ramírez Herrera will situate Ancestral Abiayala within larger conversations about the mobility of belongings, violent and otherwise, and what it might mean to care for them responsibly in museum practice and scholarly writing. 
The talk offers a behind-the-scenes look at what went into developing the Ancestral Abiayala Gallery, connecting its questions to broader intellectual debates in the field.

                    Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera
                    
                
                
                    Dr. Juliana Ramírez Herrera is Assistant Professor of Indigenous Art and Archaeology of the Ancestral Americas and of Colonial Latin American Art at the University of California, Berkeley. She specializes in the so-called small-scale societies of pre-Conquest and early colonial Panama, Colombia, the Caribbean, and Amazonia. Before joining UC Berkeley, she was a SSHRC Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Toronto and the Gardiner Museum of Ceramic Art, where she collaborated with curators Dr. Sequoia Miller, Dr. Karine Tsoumis, and Franchesca Herbert-Spence on the renovation of the Museum’s ground floor. She earned her PhD from Harvard University and her MA from the University of Toronto.

title: Club de lecture théâtre avec le Théâtre français de Toronto
location: Toronto Reference Library, Founders' Room (rez-de-chaussée)
description:
La Bibliothèque publique de Toronto et le
Théâtre français de Toronto
s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Chacun est le bienvenu au club, qu'il soit néophyte ou amateur de théâtre confirmé. Les seuls prérequis pour participer sont la curiosité et le plaisir d'échanger autour du théâtre !
Au mois d'octobre, nous allons discuter un extrait de la pièce
Rhinocéros
de Eugène Ionesco.  Le sublime se confond avec le ridicule dans ce commentaire féroce sur la condition humaine, un incontournable de tout cours de théâtre et du théâtre du 20e siècle. Une petite ville est assiégée par un citoyen rugissant qui se transforme en rhinocéros et se met à piétiner l'ordre social. À mesure que d'autres citoyens se transforment en rhinocéros, le piétinement devient écrasant, et de plus en plus de citoyens deviennent des rhinocéros. Un seul homme sain d'esprit, Bérenger, reste incapable de changer de forme et d'identité.
Rhinocéros

title: From Portfolio to Book
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Aesthetics Reading Group (John Dyck, Misssissippi State University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Aesthetics Reading Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker John Dyck, assistant professor emeritus in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Mississippi State University. 
Talk Title
The Veracity of Beauty and the Ambition of Realism 
Talk Abstract
Some have said that the beauty of some things (perhaps all things) consists in their very reality. The sense in which something is beautiful is precisely the sense in which it is real. This view declares the veracity of beauty. While such a view may seem old fashioned, I argue here that it offers crucial insights for the contemporary pursuit to understand beauty and aesthetic value in general. This view explains what we might call ambitions of realism that abound in art criticism and in our own appreciative logic: recurring praise for what is real or true. Despite its grand historical precedent, many contemporary philosophers may be wary of such a view, especially given its ties with metaphysically suspect views like Neoplatonism. To calm the metaphysically skittish, I present a version of the view that avoids not only extravagant Neoplatonist commitments but also naïve assumptions about easy epistemic access to reality. Along the way, I consider what it would mean for reality to ever constitute beauty, as it must if this view is to have a fighting chance.

title: One Last Backcountry Weekend in Frontenac
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**Fall (aka shoulder season) camping brings the serene beauty of the backcountry, without the crowds and bugs.**

At this time of year, Frontenac will be less busy and the trail into Big Clear Lake belongs mostly to us. It's a 9km hike to reach the site, working through root tangled trails and stretches of open granite typical of this stretch of the Canadian Shield. Only the most stubborn leaves will remain on the trees and you’ll enjoy long sightlines through bare branches where the canopy used to be. The pace is steady and moderate the whole way in, never technical but never quite letting up either.

We set up camp on the shore of Big Clear Lake as the light starts to drop, we get a fire going, and cook dinner together. Late October nights out here are serene, with a sky full of stars over the lake.

In the morning, we’ll take our time over breakfast before packing up and heading out along the other side of Big Salmon Lake: a different stretch of trail from the one we hiked in on, with its own look at the park before we're back where we started.

By the time we're back at the cars, you'll have had that sweet final night of the year in the backcountry.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Last Trip of the Season:** The final overnight on the calendar before WU's backcountry program pauses for winter
**Shoulder Season Solitude**: Long, quiet stretches of trail, with the lake mostly to yourselves.
**A Clear Night Sky:** Bare branches and dry autumn air make for some of the best stargazing conditions of the year at the campsite.

**Event cost: $265+HST. $70 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Lost Libraries of the Ancient World (LECTURES - 5TH ANNIVERSARY SPECIAL)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**The location of this Lecture might change in the next few months so stay tuned for more information regarding the venue! As of now the location will still be Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Bay Street until further notice.**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026/2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. The first Lecture on the Go was **Walking North America** and that was in October of 2021. Hard to believe it's been 5 years of lectures. So I wanted to do something special to celebrate 5 years of exploration.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Let's get started.

What if some of humanity's greatest discoveries were made thousands of years ago, and then lost forever?

What if entire histories, scientific breakthroughs, literary masterpieces, and eyewitness accounts of the ancient world once existed, only to disappear into the flames of war, and the collapse of civilizations?

Join me for a fascinating journey into the world's lost libraries, from the legendary Library of Alexandria to the vanished collections of ancient empires whose treasures may be lost forever.

At the heart, stands the Library of Alexandria, the most famous library in history. Founded over two thousand years ago, it sought to gather all the knowledge of the known world. Scholars from across the Mediterranean came to study astronomy, mathematics, geography, medicine, philosophy, and literature. Yet one of history's greatest mysteries remains: what happened to this remarkable institution, and what priceless knowledge disappeared with it?

Was it destroyed in a single catastrophe, or did it slowly fade away over centuries from neglect?

Beyond Alexandria, we will explore a forgotten world of lost libraries and vanished collections stretching from Mesopotamia and ancient Egypt to medieval Europe, Baghdad, and China. Discover the remarkable stories of librarians, scholars, explorers, and rulers who dedicated their lives to preserving knowledge.

We will encounter lost books, missing histories, ancient scientific works, and literary treasures that survive today only as fragments.
This lecture is an exploration of one of history's most compelling questions: What have we forgotten?

And how libraries shaped civilization and why their loss continues to fascinate us centuries later. Whether you are a lover of history, literature, archaeology, or simply enjoy a good mystery, this special Lecture on the Go will leave you wondering. What secrets of the past may still lie hidden, just waiting to be rediscovered? Fascinating indeed!

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (September 2027)

So book your plans now!

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

description:
Celebrate the beauty of autumn with this beginner-friendly watercolour workshop!
Explore the transparency and fluidity of watercolour while capturing the beauty of fall foliage. Bring your own favourite leaves or choose from samples provided by the facilitator, and learn techniques for colour application, blending and harmonizing. Create beautiful seasonal leaf studies to take home and enjoy.
 
Beginners welcome. All materials are included.
 
Saturday, October 24, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $45, TBG Members $35 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Linda Borris
Linda is a Toronto-based artist, specializing in watercolour painting techniques. She focuses on her interests in botanical studies and constantly strives to discover interesting ways to portray her work. Linda’s painting compositions depict her particular attention to detail. Her art generally consists of bright, bold colours and forms. Mostly working with florals, Linda occasionally completes a fun landscape. Her paintings’ subject matter are usually taken from her own photography images. Linda loves to share her enjoyment in the lively and vibrant world of botanical essences. Her art can be seen in both group exhibits and separate venues.
 
She is a member of the Beach Guild of Fine Art and former member of Botanical Artists of Canada.
 
Also visit Linda’s work on Instagram: @watercolourslinda

title: Botanical Printed Notebook and Prints
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of creating a customized notebook and prints!
Using the process of linocut, you’ll create a custom printed Japanese notebook and 4 fine art prints. From designing your image, through to carving and printing, our instructor will demonstrate linocut techniques and provide individual guidance. By the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with 1 unique botanical-themed notebook, 4 original prints and new printmaking skills. Beginners welcome.
 
You can create anything, so please bring photos, sketches, and designs for reference and inspiration. Your image needs to measure 4×6 inches. If you’re stuck for ideas, pressed leaves will be available.
 
Making art can be messy, please wear old clothes or an apron. Materials included.
 
Each student will receive:
 


1 Japanese notebook
1 block of soft cut lino
4 sheets of toned art paper
black printmaking ink


Saturday, October 24, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $80, TBG Members $70 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

title: The Friends of the Arthur Conan Doyle Collection: 2026 Cameron Hollyer Memorial Lecture
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground floor
description:
The Sultan and the Detective: Sherlock Holmes’ Curious Adventures in the Ottoman Empire
Historical fact: the last great Ottoman sultan, Abdülhamid II, fell asleep each night to the adventures of Sherlock Holmes, read aloud to him by a palace attendant. This unlikely obsession is the starting point for Andrew Finkel's novel
The Adventure of the Second Wife.
In this talk, Finkel explores how the world of Arthur Conan Doyle intersected with the late Ottoman Empire, and what this reveals about storytelling, translation, and the unexpected ways stories travel across languages, cultures, and empires to take on meanings the author never intended.
Andrew Finkel is a journalist and author who has reported from Turkey for major international outlets including
The Times, The Economist, TIME, CNN,
and
The New York Times
. He co-founded Platform24 (P24), an Istanbul-based NGO that supports independent journalism and freedom of expression, and is the author of
Turkey: What Everyone Needs to Know
.

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Quand la représentation sociale cède la place aux sentiments.
description:
Du Néoclassicisme à l’Académisme, de David à Ingres, les commandes de portraits furent souvent le moyen d’affirmer son rang dans la société. Du Romantisme à l’Impressionnisme, une sensibilité nouvelle se fait jour : l’on pose en communion avec la nature et non plus dans la magnificence de sa demeure, les regards traduisent des sentiments (Renoir) et non plus une volonté de puissance, les gestes sont spontanés (Degas, Manet) et non plus codifiés. Quant aux artistes, ils valorisent, dans leurs autoportraits, l’acte créateur, l’inspiration (Girodet, Delacroix), voire les tourments intérieurs (Courbet, Baudelaire).
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は5頂いております。

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

title: Toronto East Weekend Gaming @ Face-to-Face Games
description:
Toronto Heavy Boardgamers
Welcome to the Sunday meetup for Toronto Heavy Boardgamers @ Face-to-Face Games!

The purpose of this event is to meet up to play heavier / longer board games, and have fun while doing it! We will start off small and if there is sufficient interest we will add capacity for future events.

**Scheduling details:**

\- If you have a specific game that you would like to post for\, feel free to do so in comments\. In your post\, include the name of the game\, number of players needed for the game\, whether you are offering a teach or not\, and the start time \(please try to start before noon if possible\)\.

\- If you would like to join a specific game that has already been posted\, feel free to comment on it confirming your participation\. Make sure you have noted the details posted by the host\.

\- You are of course also welcome to organize / join games onsite on the day itself\, assuming sufficient players / tables are available

**Rules around COVID:**

\- Given this is a public event\, we respectfully ask that only i\) fully vaccinated individuals\, and ii\) those not exhibiting any COVID symptoms\, participate\. This requirement may change in the future based on provincial guidelines and group requirements

**Admission Fee:**

\- There are no table fees for this event

title: Paradise Opening Night Reception
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
In the multimedia exhibit, Paradise , which includes sculpture, print, and video, Japanese Canadian artists and childhood friends Emma Nishimura and Mitchell Akiyama grapple with their family histories of internment. They consider how utopian worlds are created through resilience and displacement, while urging us to remember that utopia for some may not be utopia for all. Find out more about the exhibit here . Please join us at our opening reception for a chance to take in this meaningful show and to meet the artists! Light refreshments will be served.

Categories: Community Event, Social, Exhibition

title: Author Talk featuring Sally Hayden
location: Ben McNally Books
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books for a special evening with journalist Sally Hayden, former winner of the Irish Book of the Year (
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
), and author of
This is Also a Love Story: A Reporter's Search for Goodness in a Cruel World
.
Sally with be joined in conversation by journalist Katie Engelhart.
Order a copy of
This is Also a Love Story
here.
About the Book
An acclaimed reporter takes us on an unforgettable journey, capturing the human capacity for love and connection against all odds.
We live in an era defined by crisis—whether it be war and displacement, climate collapse, or growing inequality, and how the powerful profit from violence and exploitation. Celebrated foreign correspondent Sally Hayden has spent her career on the frontlines, uncovering some of the darkest moments of our time. Yet even in the face of unimaginable adversity, she’s witnessed the incredible goodness of regular people.
In
This Is Also a Love Story
, Hayden reexamines catastrophe through the love stories she has come across. She introduces us to a mother in northeast Nigeria who risks everything to save her daughter from forced marriage to Boko Haram militants, and to a group of Syrian women who have tirelessly searched for their missing spouses and children, while launching a call for justice. We meet a couple separated by the Russian invasion of Ukraine and read letters from the bereaved to the dead, still being written over a decade after the tsunami that devastated Japan. Through these stories, which crisscross the globe, from Uganda to Lebanon, Ghana, Rwanda and Iraq, she challenges us to reconsider what it means to be alive on this planet today.
What if news was recounted through the prism of the actions and decisions people take for those they love? Would it become harder to dehumanize those who seem different to us?
This Is Also a Love Story
dares us to recognize how innate generosity and self-sacrifice can be found in even the most difficult of times, and—as a result—to question what might be needed to create a better world.
About the Author
Sally Hayden is an Irish journalist focused on migration, conflict, and humanitarian crises. Sally’s work has been featured by
The New York Times, the Irish Times, The Washington Post, Financial Times, The Guardian, CNN International, Al Jazeera, Time, BBC
, and other outlets across the world. Sally’s first book
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
was the winner of the Orwell Prize and the Irish Book of the Year, and was a finalist for the Baillie Gifford Prize and the New York Public Library’s Helene Bernstein Book Award for excellence in journalism.

Mark of the Vampire

Synopsis:
Mad Love
: Doctor Gogol is a renowned surgeon who is obsessed with stage performer Yvonne Orlac. So much so that he he actually goes to the theater every evening just to see her. He is disappointed to learn from her that she is leaving the show to join her husband, famed pianist Stephen Orlac, on a much delayed honeymoon. The Orlacs no sooner set off than they are involved in an accident where Stephen's hands are crushed. She begs Dr. Gogol to do anything to save her husband. He decides to graft new hands to replace those that are crushed and uses those from a recently executed prisoner, Rollo the Knife Thrower. When Stephen regains the use of his hands those around him find that he has also undergone a personality change and is now prone to violent fits of temper. He's also very good at knife throwing.
Mark of the Vampire
: After Sir Karell Borotin is found dead in his study, drained of his blood, the local doctor determines that he was killed by a vampire. The coroner and police Inspector Neumann dismiss the suggestion but a year later, Sir Karell's daughter is attacked and bite marks are found on her throat. Neumann calls in the eminent Professor Zelin who thinks the story of vampires is true. The locals are convinced that Count Mora and his daughter Luna are the perpetrators of the crime, creatures of the night that can turn themselves into bats. There may be another solution however and the Professor sets a trap.

Reclayming Space to Build Community            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events

6:00 pm – 8:00 pm
 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    For ages 18+ 
How do we nurture love for ourselves, one another, and our world? 
The simple practice of breath connects us with our shared humanity. Together, we’ll explore how to breathe slower, relaxing into the core of our body, breathing low and slow with clay to be in rhythm with all things. Through clay, breath, and presence we remember a sense of belonging. Moving with the malleability of clay, we connect with our own spirit of generosity and possibility. As a community of practice, we generate spaciousness for all beings, past, present, and future. 
Join us in clayming a sustainable, thriving future for our communities and future generations and, in the process, share wisdom about what thriving means to us now. In this 4-week workshop guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, explore the dance between breath and clay through a series of hand-building exercises designed to awaken you the present moment and encourage you to experience through your senses. Moving with one body, one breath, one human family, we learn to interrupt habits of separation and create space for all to thrive. 

At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

description:
Woodworking Level 2 at TTLMakerspace

 
 
 Note: This course requires previous completion of Intro to Woodworking

 In this course at TTLMakerspace, you will use and expand upon the skills learned in Intro Woodworking. Working in a small group with dedicated instructor, you'll expand your skills in two practical box-building projects designed to develop deeper understanding of woodworking.

 In this followup to Woodworking Intro students advance their skills into more sophisticated use of both power tools and hand tools. During the course two projects are created that reveal techniques for creating mitred joints, splines, inlays, lap joints, and finishing techniques.

 Build up confidence in the shop and learn new, valuable woodworking techniques.

 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 

 Schedule : 

 Six three-hour weekly classes, Tuesdays 10am to 1pm. 

 Outcomes : 

 At the end of this course you will have achieved the following goals: 

 
- Become more comfortable milling rough lumber 

- Complete mitered corners 

- Complete box joints 

- Use a spline jig 

- Complete inlays 

- Install hinges 

- Apply finishes 

- Learn how to plan projects efficiently with minimal waste 

 
 Following this course, you'll be certified to use the woodshop. And you'll be able to join the growing community of TTL Makers sharing knowledge on our Discord community.

Useful for: furniture, cabinets, organisers, cutting-boards

Prompting Skills

description:
Come join the readers at Long Branch each month. We share opinions and thoughts of the books selected. For the Month of October take a look at "Children of the Moon" by Anthony DeSa.
From critically-acclaimed author Anthony De Sa, a raw and compelling story of love, war and the differences that both divide and unite us. In the wispy grasslands of Tanzania in the 1950s, a Maasai woman gives birth to a miracle. The other villagers see the baby as a curse. The baby--a daughter, named Kibo--has skin as white as bone, and from her first moments on earth, she is forced to claim her life in spite of the violence she incites. As she grows, Kibo sheds her identity to become Liloe, and then Po, continuously trying to adjust herself so that she can fit into the world around her. Further south, in Portuguese-controlled Mozambique, a young boy, Ezequiel, has been adopted by two missionaries. Zeca, too, struggles with a lack of acceptance. Not recognized by his Portuguese father's community, or by his Makonde mother's tribe, Zeca lives his life on the borders of both worlds. And when civil war erupts in Mozambique, Zeca must choose what--and who--he is willing to leave behind

title: Seagoing Women: Author Sara Donnelly & Panel Talk with Water Women At Work
description:
Journalist, mariner, and author of
Seagoing Women: At Work
,
Sara Donnelly
, creates captivating portraits of thirty-three women who have built remarkable careers on the water, everything from tugboat operators and commercial fishers to naval architects and whale researchers.
Through vivid first-person accounts, this panel talk will offer a rare glimpse at offshore life: the physical demands, long stretches away from home, ingenuity required in unpredictable conditions and deep sense of purpose shared by those whose lives are tied to the ocean.
Moderated by Donnelly, this panel talk will feature:
Ocean Rutherford
- West Coast Canadian mariner, tugboat deckhand, commercial fisher, and children's book author from Prince Rupert, British Columbia. Ocean Rutherford made headlines in December 2023 as part of the first all-female tugboat crew in SAAM Towage Canada's 70-year history.
Weyla Chipp
s - After raising four children and working as an education assistant in the Sooke School District, Weyla Chipps of the Scia’new First Nation seized the chance to train for a new life at sea: working on anchor handlers in the North Sea and embarking on adventures through the Bermuda Triangle and along the Panama Canal.
Connie Bell-Irving -
Originally from Australia, Connie Bell-Irving became the first woman on the BC coast to command oil barges and later the first in Canada to receive Transport Canada's full endorsement as Supervisor of an Oil Transfer Operation. Today she is part of HaiSea Marine in Kitimat, the world's first partnership of its kind between the Haisla Nation and Seaspan, operating the most sustainable tug fleet in the industry.
Join in to be inspired by the stories and career experiences that highlights determination, skill and resilience in a profession defined by adventure, challenge and reward.
Presented as part of Women's History Month. Please note that the program time is

title: The Lede: A Live Editorial Meeting Experience
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and the Canadian Journalism Foundation present a special Media Literacy week event!
Three journalists. One front page. Only one story leads.
The Lede pulls back the curtain on a process most people never see: how editors weigh impact, timeliness, public interest and audience relevance under pressure, in real time.
Three journalists from The Globe and Mail, Canada's national newspaper, deputy head of investigations Robyn Doolittle, politics and economy editor Ryan MacDonald and senior visuals editor Solana Cain, will each pitch the story they believe deserves the lead position in tomorrow's news. Editor-in-chief David Walmsley will question their assumptions, challenge their reasoning and make the final call, live, in front of the audience.
The audience does not just watch. Before Walmsley announces his decision, they vote on which story should lead, then see how their judgment compares with his.
Join us for a chance to understand not just what the news is, but how it gets made, and to walk away a sharper, more critical reader of it.
About this event’s guests:
David Walmsley
is
The Globe and Mail
’s editor-in-chief and the current president of the World Editors Forum. He is the co-creator of World News Day, a global day of education involving more than 1,000 publishers across 100 countries explaining the role of journalism and how it can make the world a better place. Under his editorship, The Globe has won the annual Canadian Michener Award for meritorious public service journalism five times and has dominated the annual National Newspaper Awards.
Robyn Doolittle
is the deputy head of investigations at
The Globe and Mail
. Doolittle came to
The Globe
in 2014 to join the investigative unit. After a decade on the i-Team, she spent time in the Report on Business covering corporate law. She has investigated political and business corruption, a series of shootings and arsons targeting Canadian waste giant GFL, the Hockey Canada scandal, gender inequities in the workforce and Canada’s broken freedom of information system as part of the Secret Canada project. Her two books, “Had It Coming – What’s Fair In The Age of #MeToo?,” and “Crazy Town: The Rob Ford Story,” were both national bestsellers.
Ryan MacDonald
is the editor of politics and economy at
The Globe and Mail
, leading a talented team of reporters covering the intersection of business and economic policy, including energy, finance, trade and fiscal matters. Since joining
The Globe
in 2007, MacDonald has held multiple editorial positions and was notably part of the team that won the 2022 CJF Climate Solutions Reporting Award for its narrative-shifting stories on how to re-engineer Canada’s economy to adapt to and capitalize on climate change. Prior to joining
The Globe
, MacDonald served as the national editor at the
Ottawa Citizen
.
Solana Cain
is a senior visuals editor at
The Globe and Mail
, Canada’s national newspaper. She joined
The Globe
through the 2019 summer program, quickly distinguishing herself as a perceptive and composed photo editor. In 2020, Cain helped establish Room Up Front, a mentorship initiative supporting BIPOC photojournalists. The program received a special citation at the 2023 National Newspaper Awards for its significant contribution to Canadian journalism. A dedicated mentor and educator, she actively advises emerging photographers and lectures at Toronto Metropolitan University, Sheridan College, and Loyalist College.

Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.

title: Marlon James: The Disappearers
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents Booker Prize-winning author Marlon James in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
In his triumphant return to the Jamaica of his Booker Prize-winning
A Brief History of Seven Killings
, Marlon James delivers
The Disappearers
, an epic, unflinching novel about survival in the aftermath of violence. Written with the language-rich, urgent style that has made James one of the most acclaimed novelists working today, this is a story of men forced to make impossible compromises to survive a society that demands their erasure.
At once a detective story and a searing sociocultural history,
The Disappearers
plunges into the tragic, ongoing consequences of violent homophobia, rendering its characters' inner lives with the vivid imagery, sharp dialogue, and unrelenting energy that have defined James's celebrated body of work.
Join one of the most acclaimed novelists of his generation, in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee, for an evening exploring rage, resilience, and the price of queer solidarity in a world built to deny it.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: Colour & Atmosphere
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Jesse Wente: Tough Lies
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Award-winning author Jesse Wente shares his highly-anticipated new book exploring how we can heal from colonialism.
In Tough Lies, Wente explores his own healing path and how it informs what he sees as necessary for reconciliation between Nations, asking us to consider several pressing questions.
What does healing from colonialism look like for First Nations? What about non-Indigenous people? What are the barriers to this healing, and what can we do to move past them?
Through a lens of healing and anti-colonial thought, Wente examines his reaction to incidents that have hit close to home, chronicling his personal journey and what it has taught him about the present and future of reconciliation in Canada.
Jesse Wente speaks with professor Kim Anderson about Tough Lies and the path for healing between Nations.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jesse Wente
Kim Anderson

title: Magnifica Humanitas: Choosing Humanity in the AI Revolution
description:
— A Symposium on Putting Pope Leo’s “AI Encyclical” into Practice 







October 30-31, 2026 (Fri/Sat), 10:30am – 5:00pm 



Father Madden Hall (in Carr Hall, 100 St. Joseph St) 



Free admission / Lunch included: Register now 



How do we maintain our humanity and agency in a world that increasingly revolves around AI? 



From workplaces to social media feeds, from breakthroughs in healthcare research to that question you Googled last night, AI seems to be permeating every aspect of our lives. But as the ways we think, work, live, and act are being rapidly transformed, how do we protect and nurture those parts of our humanity that matter most—our dignity, our agency, our creativity and moral commitments? 



Join us as we discern our stakes in the current AI revolution through the lens of Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical.” Through two days of panels, discussions, and workshops, we will explore how the Pope uses Catholic social teaching to engage with the structural realities of AI, and consider our own practical responses to his call to prioritise human dignity over unrestricted AI development. 



By asking practical questions about AI in light of Magnifica Humanitas, this symposium will help us engage critically and faithfully with changing technologies in our own lives, work, and service to the world. Whether you are new to the conversation and wanting to learn more or are already confronting pressing issues around AI, we welcome you to join us in this timely dialogue on navigating the emerging AI frontier. 



__________ 



Magnifica Humanitas Online Reading Group 



Monday evenings (7-8pm) from Sep. 14-Oct. 19 



UPDATE: sign-ups for the reading group have now closed. 



Are you interested in Pope Leo’s “AI encyclical,” but daunted by the thought of reading it alone? Have you been tempted to ask ChatGPT for a summary? Join us instead for this virtual reading group and explore the encyclical in conversation with others. Over 6 weekly sessions, Dr. Ren Ito will facilitate discussions of each chapter of Magnifica Humanitas. Participants will build an understanding of the encyclical’s key arguments, and will learn to engage with current issues of new technology through the lens of Catholic social teaching. 



Participants will also have the opportunity to present reflections on and takeaways from the encyclical during a session of our October 30-31 Magnifica Humanitas symposium.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: Demonlover
description:
In this second instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, critic Saffron Maeve and director Pascal Plante discuss Demonlover, the 2002 French neo-noir thriller film directed by Olivier Assayas. Exploring the damaging effects of media and modern desensitization to violence, the film has gained a cult-following in recent years.
About this event's guests:
Saffron Maeve
is a Toronto-based critic, film curator, and researcher. A regular contributor to The Globe and Mail, her writing has also appeared in numerous publications.
Pascal Plante
is a Canadian film director and screenwriter from Quebec, whose debut feature film, Fake Tattoos, premiered in 2017. His second film, Nadia, Butterfly, premiered in 2020 in the official selection of the Cannes Film Festival. His third feature film, Red Rooms, garnered widespread critical acclaim.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.

title: Artists in the Library: Origami Lotus Flowers
location: Thorncliffe, Program Room
description:
This is a six-part workshop series that creates a space for exploring belonging and not belonging through conversation and hands-on art-making. Guided by reflective questions, participants engage in practices such as origami with washi, drawing, dyeing, and writing, using the lotus as a shared symbol of transformation and resilience across cultures. The workshops foster an inclusive, supportive environment, particularly for those who feel marginalized or disconnected. The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
The workshops are open to youth, ages 13-17, and require no prior artistic experience.

We are a fun, friendly and kind group of people mostly in our 20s, 30s and 40s. Beginners are welcome! We are a very inclusive and social group and we teach people how to play games they have not played before :)

We provide a variety of 40+ board games. The games usually take 5 or 10 minutes to learn and 30 to 60 minutes to play.
