title: 2026 Duende International Flamenco Festival: Masterclasses
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
This special series of masterclasses offers dancers a rare opportunity to learn with three extraordinary flamenco artists, Óscar de los Reyes, Carmen Talegona, and El Yiyo.

Each workshop offers participants a deeper understanding of the art form’s power, precision, musicality, and emotional truth. The three artists brings a distinct voice, lineage, and approach, guiding dancers toward greater technical clarity, expressive range, and connection to rhythm, structure, and cante. Together, these masterclasses create a rich encounter with flamenco as a living, evolving art form — one that honours tradition while continuing to move boldly into the future.

Open to intermediate, advanced, and professional-level dancers, the workshops offer an inspiring environment for growth, exchange, and artistic discovery.

title: Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World
location: Aga Khan Museum, Massey Hall, Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium
description:
Celebrate flamenco’s global transformation through cross-cultural exchange at the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World.

From November 18 to 22, experience the vibrant evolution of flamenco — from its regional roots in Andalusia to a dynamic global art form shaped by cross-cultural exchange. This year’s lineup spans both traditional flamenco from Andalusia and innovative collaborations at the crossroads of qawwali and Persian muqam, tracing the art form’s evolution from its regional roots to a global practice.

title: Hope in Action: Building Hope: Reimagining Institutions for Human Flourishing (Continuing Education Free Webinar)
description:
In a time of precarity, fragmentation, burnout, and democratic uncertainty, what would be possible if we stepped outside of the constrictions of scarcity and austerity and oriented toward abundance to reimagine how our public-serving higher education institutions can be places where hope can become a force for collective renewal? 



In this webinar, Dr. Jessica Riddell (professor of Early Modern Literature at Bishop’s University and founder of the Hope Circuits Institute) will join Dr. David Sylvester (President and Vice-Chancellor of the University of St. Michael’s College) to discuss the transformative role that hope plays in building vibrant institutions.  



Drawing on her work with the Hope Circuits Institute and her forthcoming book, Hope Circuits Illuminated: Conversations with Luminaries Amid Collapse, Dr. Riddell will share practical tools, reflections and insights from engaging in thousands of hours of conversations with scholars, students, presidents, staff, artists, and public thinkers to explore how public educational institutions can reclaim their civic purpose and embrace the complexity of our world to imagine new futures. 



Part of the Hope in Action speaker series from USMC CE



Join Continuing Education at the University of St. Michael’s College for a free speaker series exploring how hope becomes action in sustainability, leadership, social impact, spirituality, education, technology, and the arts. 



Hope is not wishful thinking. It is the decision to engage with our world’s most urgent challenges and work toward meaningful change , from climate and culture to how we live our values in our workplaces and communities. 



Hope in Action brings together innovators, faculty, alumni, and leaders who are meeting urgent challenges with clarity, courage, and purpose. 



Come to be inspired. Leave ready to act.

title: Tutankhamun: The Sensational Discovery - Part 2
location: North York Central Library, Room 1 (2nd floor)
description:
This year marks an important anniversary in the history of Egyptology. On November 4th, 2026, it will be 104 years since Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon discovered the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun in 1922 - a discovery that continues to capture the public imagination.
Nearly a year after the complete collection went on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo on November 1, 2025, Egyptologist Sherine ElSebaie will take audiences back to the time of its discovery. Following the footsteps of the excavators, she will conclude the story of the discovery and explore the remarkable objects found in the burial chamber and the treasury during the excavation of 1923.
Registration is encouraged but not required.

title: Native Plant Series: Right Plant in the Right Place
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging workshop where you’ll learn about biodiversity, native plants and how to enhance your garden!
While other sessions in the Native Plant Series explore how to grow native plants from seed, this session focuses on choosing the right plants for your garden and finding the best place to plant them. The right plant in the right place is key to growing a successful garden. Whether your space is sunny or shady, dry or exposed to road salt, there are native plants suited to every condition.
 
We’ll also share local sources for native plants, shrubs and trees. Fall is the perfect time to plan additions to your garden for next year, so come learn how to make the best choices for your space!
 
Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 to 8 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.

Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Rachel Cusk: Life of M
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Critically acclaimed author Rachel Cusk shares her irresistible new novel.
Life of M introduces us to movie star M, one of the most recognizable faces of our time, whose image has been ubiquitous since she was a child.
With such fame, her life has the appearance of freedom: people are instantly obliging, spaces are altered to accommodate her, time can be rearranged. M may live in the same places as real people. She may meet her friends or collect her children from school or walk her dogs as they do. But it seems the rules of reality have melted away.
Now, a writer has decided to pay close attention to M’s life in the hope of understanding who she really is. It is hard not to feel ugly next to M, hard not to feel insignificant. But what truths―about the very experience of living―might this proximity allow the writer to briefly capture?
Rachel Cusk speaks with Sheila Heti about Life of M, an astonishing new novel about fame, power, beauty, and truth
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

Part of the Aga Khan Museum’s 12th annual Duende International Flamenco Festival: Flamenco and the World, join us for a film screening that celebrates the legacy of Farruquito, one of the greatest flamenco dancers of this century.

Farruquito is celebrated as the finest flamenco dancer of his generation. He belongs to a legendary dynasty of bailaores (dancers). At only 20, he was already at the height of his success, captivating audiences around the globe from New York to Tokyo – with his extraordinary talent, yet the shadows of his family’s tumultuous history loomed large.

The film follows Farruquito’s journey through triumph and tragedy, focusing on a pivotal moment that changes everything — a tragic accident that leads to the death of a pedestrian and lands him in prison. This harrowing experience forces him to confront the demons of his past and the heavy burden of his family’s legacy.

location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an introduction to Sleep Qigong & Self-Acupressure!
Sleep issues can occur at different times during our lives in a variety of ways and for different reasons. You might have trouble falling asleep; perhaps you can fall asleep easily but wake up several times throughout the night; you might fall asleep but wake up too early feeling you haven’t slept quite enough; or you suffer from insomnia. Stress, anxiety, depression, age, worry, and other factors can all contribute to sleep complications.
 
In this session, I will demonstrate and guide you through some holistic and non-invasive ways to deal with sleep issues. They will include simple self-acupressure, gentle qigong, helpful tips, and calming breathing exercises.
 
Whether you experience occasional or chronic sleep problems, this session can provide you with some alternative ways to deal with it.
Thursday, November 9, 10 to 11:30 a.m.
Registration: Public $25, TBG Member $20 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About David Leopold
Sifu David Leopold has been practicing, studying, researching and teaching martial and healing arts since 1994.
 
In 1999, Sifu David achieved his black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu. Since 1999, Sifu David has received numerous certifications in Tachi and weapon forms, and seven Qigong routines. In 2009, Sifu David received his Usui Reiki master certification from the Naturopathic School of Medicine in Toronto.
 
In 2012, Sifu David travelled to China to compete in the International Wushi Competition in Shanghai. He brought home 2 gold and a bronze medal.
 
By combining all these modalities and experiences, Sifu David brings a unique style of teaching that includes technique, philosophy, and practicality. Sify David’s approach to teaching is relaxed and he believes Taichi and Qigong practice should be useful in everyday life and enjoyable to do.
 
Sifu David has a passion for martial and healing arts. His holistic approach to wellness includes physical, emotional, spiritual and nutritional well-being. Sifu David continues to improve his skills as a practitioner, teacher/ mentor, and hopes to teach for the rest of his life.
 
Sifu David’s words of wisdom:
 
“To be a master of what you do, you must first be a master unto yourself.”

title: Nov 19 - Visualizing and Debugging Hugging Face's LeRobot Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop is a hands-on tour of what actually breaks when you load real LeRobot datasets, and how Voxel51's native LeRobot support in FiftyOne catches it.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 19, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/lerobot-workshop-november-19-2026)**

Robot learning data doesn't look like the data that trains most vision-language models. It's temporal, low-dimensional in the parts that matter most, embodiment-specific, and expensive to collect, and increasingly, it's shipped in Hugging Face's LeRobot format. But packaging robot data consistently isn't the same as being able to see it: episodes hide broken metadata, silently dropped sensor modalities, and mismatched schemas between robots that look identical on paper.

Starting from the core differences that make robot data hard (temporal structure, proprioception, action grounding, embodiment heterogeneity, data scarcity), we'll move into live debugging: a metadata bug that broke multiple dataset imports, sensor streams that vanish without an error, and two robots running an identical benchmark whose data is structurally incompatible. By the end, you'll know what to check before you trust a LeRobot dataset, and how to actually look inside one.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: The Ishizue Award Dinner 2026
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
The JCCC Board of Directors is pleased to announce that the 8th Ishizue Award and accompanying dinner will be held on Thursday November 19, 2026. The Ishizue Award acknowledges and expresses our appreciation and respect to members or friends who have made exceptional contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. The name Ishizue, meaning cornerstone or foundation, pays tribute to the 75 families who, at significant personal financial risk, guaranteed the original mortgage on the JCCC at 123 Wynford Drive in the early 1960’s. These families provided the foundation upon which the JCCC was built, and their support for the JCCC will forever be recognized as the cornerstone for who we are as a community. The recipients of this annual award are a very distinguished group of people who have each made significant life contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. They are: Ken Fukushima Harry Kawabe Akiko Maruoka David Ohashi (Post humous) Connie Sugiyama David Tsubouchi We cordially invite you to honour these distinguished award recipients at an intimate and elegant dinner on Thursday November 19th at 6:30pm at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. Black tie optional. Tickets are $180 each (plus HST) . Maximum of 10 guests per table. To purchase tickets please order through the button below or in person at the JCCC, starting September 21, 2026, and ending November 9, 2026. Please contact Sharon Marubashi for any further information by email or phone (647-291-4751). On behalf of all of the directors of the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, we look forward to spending a special evening of recognition and celebration together. Purchase Ticket

title: Qawwali Flamenco
location: Massey Hall, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
From Pakistan to Andalusia, musical traditions have crossed paths, met, nourished one another, and blended so thoroughly that between the volcanic power and virtuosity of qawwali singing and the hypnotic lyricism of flamenco, distances fade and similarities naturally emerge.

Qawwali Flamenco marks the long-awaited return of the celebrated collaboration between Pakistani qawwali master Faiz Ali Faiz and flamenco guitar virtuoso Juan Gómez “Chicuelo.”

Following their acclaimed first collaboration a decade ago, Faiz and Gómez reunite to deepen a remarkable artistic dialogue. The first chapter of their Qawwali Flamenco journey explored the relationship between human beings and their beloved; this new creation turns toward the connection between humanity and the divine.

title: Adaptive Ceramic Histories
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Adaptive Ceramic Histories                                                                          
        
    




	

	

	


			
Events
	









	

    
        
             
                
                    

November 20, 2026 – March 29, 2027
The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation Hall. Ground Floor
Included with admission. Free for Gardiner Members.



                
                    
    



    
         
    




	


  Get Tickets



  Become a Member






    
         
    




	



    
        
             
                
                    Curated by Alexandra Box, Gardiner Museum Curatorial Resident 
Engage in an exploration of materially mediated dynamics of care and adaption. Adaptive Ceramic Histories presents an expansive way of looking at histories of medical and adaptive ceramics created for sick or disabled users. The exhibition invites you to delve into the design of care from the vantage point of users, departing from traditional histories of medicine centering on medical professionals. Instead, it considers the possibilities of pleasure and metaphor to build a more fulsome knowledge of patient care to craft the future. 
Adaptive Ceramic Histories features objects from the Gardiner Museum’s permanent collection alongside loans to highlight the importance of ceramic materials at different moments in the history of Western medicine from the 17th century to the present day. 
The Gardiner Museum Curatorial Residency is made possible through the generous support of the Rebanks Family. 

                
                    
    





    
         
    




    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    About the Curator
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box
                    
                
                
                    Alexandra Box is an arts professional and artist. She has been awarded fellowships and artist residencies through Medalta Potteries, Salt Spring Arts Council, and Point Gallery. Alexandra is a curatorial participant in the Knowledge Incubator & Mentorship Initiative through Redefine Arts. Her writing has been published by Hearth, Peripheral Review, and The Capilano Review. Alexandra serves on the Board at Forest City Gallery and is a contributor to the Media Collaboratory. She holds a BFA (2020) in ceramics and curatorial practices from Emily Carr University and an MA (2024) in Art History from the University of Toronto.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

Renowned Turkish novelist and Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk joins celebrated museum and cultural planning leader, Gail Lord, for an extraordinary conversation about one of the most singular acts of imagination in contemporary literature and museology: the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Conceived in tandem with his acclaimed novel of the same name, Pamuk's museum houses the fictional world of his characters Kemal and Füsun in a real, physical space — a small house in Istanbul filled with everyday objects, each one tied to a moment in the novel. The result is a haunting blur between fiction and reality, where a love story lives on not only on the page, but in glass display cases, drawers, and rooms visitors can walk through.
How does one curate a museum for people who never existed? What does it mean to give physical form to memory, longing, and melancholy — the very textures of a novel? And what challenges arise when an author becomes a museum-maker, translating narrative into space, object, and atmosphere?
Orhan Pamuk sits down with Gail Lord, co-founder of Lord Cultural Resources and one of the world's leading museum planners, to discuss the twin creation of the novel and the museum, the ethereal act of turning fiction into physical experience, and what he hoped visitors would feel wandering through the rooms of a story. The conversation will also turn to Pamuk's evolving philosophy of museums — the ideas first laid out in his "Modest Manifesto for Museums" — exploring his belief in small, intimate institutions that honor individual and everyday stories over the grand, monumental narratives so often privileged by national museums.
The discussion will also look ahead to Pamuk's second museum project, currently in development, in which he continues to explore the relationship between storytelling, memory, and collected objects. Building on the foundations laid by the Museum of Innocence, this new endeavor promises to further test the boundaries between literature and lived space, offering fresh insight into how narrative can be translated into an immersive, tangible experience.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab makes its world premiere as a bold new multidisciplinary performance celebrating the enduring connections between cultures through oral and artistic traditions. Led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri, the Amir Amiri Ensemble, featuring Óscar de los Reyes and Esperanza Soria, the performance brings together Canadian and Spanish Andalusian artists in a powerful artistic dialogue. Connected through centuries of migration, poetry, rhythm, and memory, the performance explores a shared cultural legacy while embracing new creative expression. The essentials of flamenco are all present: voice, complex rhythm, and dance.

This presentation ultimately asks how music travels through history, how cultures reshape one another, and how artists continue to carry ancient knowledge into contemporary life. The project seeks to illuminate the enduring connections between Persian and Andalusian artistic worlds, while creating a contemporary performance grounded in research, artistic integrity, and shared humanity.

title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:

This panel discussion will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it.
Featuring:
Alex Olson
, Director of University of Toronto’s Centre for Analytics & AI Engineering
Khasir Hean
, Founder of Technologists for Democracy, Machine Learning engineer

title: Flamenco: Made in Canada presents Duende Al Nur
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Duende al Nur , meaning “Duende toward the light,” is an immersive flamenco work where light, shadow and fire transform the dancing body.

Performed on a luminous plexiglass platform, the piece explores light as a sacred, living force rising from beneath the dancer. From darkness, the body is awakened by illumination. Breath becomes pulse, pulse becomes rhythm, and rhythm becomes flamenco. Through footwork, castanets, zills, breath and silence, Carmen Romero moves through a ritual journey of awakening and renewal. Rooted in the emotional power of duende and the Arabic resonance of nur, the work becomes a passage through memory, prayer, rhythm and transformation.

The work draws from flamenco’s emotional intensity, rhythmic complexity and theatrical power while opening the performance space to Arabic resonance, sacred illumination and immersive sound. Rather than presenting cultural influence literally, Duende al Nur approaches these elements as echoes, atmospheres and poetic points of connection.

title: Vote Now for Our November Pick!
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

In prepping our November Book Survey winner, Iain M. Banks’ *Against a Dark Background*, I found that reviews are fairly split, with both sides generally agreeing that there are much better Banks novels to read. I do my research before a book makes it onto the survey, but this one got by me. Let’s honor Banks’ second-place win on our recent contemporary survey and choose a different novel from this prolific sci fi writer.

[Take a moment to vote on which Iain M. Banks novel we’ll read in November.](https://forms.gle/9mSFuPV3dQyiHWfm8) The survey closes on Thursday, September 10th at 5pm EST.

A reminder that Book Club takes a break each October, so while these novels have fairly large page counts, we’ll essentially have two months to read our pick. All of the options below are part of Banks’ Culture series and, as we found when we read *The Player of Games*, each novel offers a window into a much larger universe, so we don't have to start with the first book in the series.

Cheers,

Jon

title: Los Magníficos
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
“Los Magníficos” is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the greatness of contemporary flamenco. Five outstanding artists come together in a unique performance where singing, dance, guitar, and piano reach their highest expression.

Sandra Carrasco, one of the most important voices of the moment, takes us to the very heart of flamenco. David de Arahal captivates audiences with his mastery of the guitar, while Andrés Barrios transforms the piano into pure emotion. Dancer “El Yiyo” embodies the power and intensity of flamenco, joined by Carmen “La Talegona,” whose artistry and magnetic stage presence bring elegance, strength, and depth to this extraordinary encounter.

Prepare for an intense and magnetic journey, where energy and sensitivity intertwine in an explosion of talent. “ Los Magníficos” is not just a performance; it’s a unique opportunity to witness the union of some of the finest artists of our time in a moment destined to remain forever in the memory of flamenco art.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.

title: ABCD Reads Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with [HOST TBC] at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honoring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

description:
Join us on Wednesday afternoon at the library for a screening of One False Move movie.
A small-town police chief conceals an explosive secret. A pair of ruthless drug dealers leave a bloody trail in their wake as they make their way from Los Angeles to Arkansas. And an enigmatic woman is caught in the middle. The way these desperate lives converge becomes a masterclass in slow-burn tension thanks to the nuanced direction of Carl Franklin, whose haunting debut feature travels a crooked road across America’s most fraught divisions—urban and rural, Black and white—while imbuing noir conventions with a wrenching emotional depth.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.
We encourage you to review the privacy statements of each tool prior to attending this program:

title: Financial Workshops for Seniors
location: Queen/Saulter
description:
Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario, learn more about government programs, benefits and eligibility criteria for seniors. These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.

title: How Pleasant to Know Mr. Lear
location: Mount Pleasant, Basement program room
description:
Dennis Duffy, Professor Emeritus, Department of English, University of Toronto, discusses the genius of Edward Lear as a painter and poet, the great joiner of oil painting and printed nonsense.
Lear was a singular eccentric in his bespoke but loosely-fitting suits and his runcible hat, he created work placing him among the finest of graphic cartoonists and satirists. This presentation explores that jagged world that he made up for himself, in order to preserve his own complex selfhood.

We're wrapping up our 2026 Entrepreneur in Residence program with a final session on launching your business. title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: We're All Going to the World's Fair
description:
In this third instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, crime writer Kathleen Hale and film critic Willow Maclay discuss Jane Schoenbrun's coming-of-age psychological horror film, We're All Going to the World's Fair alongside host Adam Nayman.
About this event's guests:
Kathleen Hale
is a crime writer based in Los Angeles. Her reporting has been featured in Vanity Fair, among other outlets. Slenderman is her first true crime book.
Willow Maclay
is a freelance film critic stationed in St. John's, Newfoundland. She has written for outlets such as The Village Voice, Ebert Voices, Cinemascope Magazine, and more. She is also the co-author of Corpses, Fools and Monsters: An Examination of Transgender Cinema.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
Corpses, Fools and Monsters

title: Holiday Succulent Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us this holiday season and create a one-of-a-kind succulent!
Celebrate the festive season with a delightful holiday-inspired succulent arranging workshop! In this creative and relaxing session, you’ll design a beautiful succulent arrangement in a charming birch-lined tin planter—perfect for adding a touch of natural elegance to your holiday décor or gifting to someone special.
 
Guided by a succulent expert, you’ll learn tips and tricks for arranging succulents with a seasonal flair, including techniques for layering textures, balancing colours, and incorporating winter-inspired accents.
 
All materials are provided, including a birch-lined tin planter, premium succulents, specialty soil, and care instruction cards to ensure your arrangement stays vibrant through the holiday season and beyond.
 
Join us for this festive workshop and leave with a stunning centrepiece that captures the warmth and beauty of the holidays!
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11 a.m.
Public $55, TBG Members $50 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Canadian Succulents
Molly is the owner and operator of the small business Canadian Succulents. Canadian Succulents creates floral arrangements using entirely succulents and cacti plants. They not only arrange and design all of the creations, but also grow all the plants that can be found in them as well. They operate out of a greenhouse just northeast of the city, where they grow over 300 varieties of succulents and cacti. They grow and create these designs for wedding centrepieces and favours, corporate events and gifting, and hotel and office greenery.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Pressed Flower Candle Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a morning of hands-on pressed flower candle making!
Discover the simple, satisfying craft of flower pressing and transform a plain pillar candle into a one-of-a-kind keepsake. Using warm palette knives to gently melt pressed flowers directly into the wax, you’ll learn a technique that’s part botanical art, part patience. Choose from a variety of pressed flowers to design your own arrangement. Beginners welcome.
 
Each attendee will receive one 6″ white pillar candle, a full selection of pressed flowers to choose from, and step-by-step guidance on using heated palette knives safely to melt your design into the wax.
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11:30 a.m.

About Epiphanie Belanger

title: Painting Botanical Cast Ornaments from Garden Blooms
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Learn how to create your own plant-based pigments and paint one-of-a-kind botanical cast ornaments!
Want to give a holiday gift that is not mass produced in a factory? Looking for a calming experience that beats the hustle and bustle? Join botanical artist Rebecca Fortin for an afternoon of natural paint-making and ornament painting.
 
Under Rebecca’s guidance, you’ll explore how to create colour pigments from local botanicals, such as goldenrod, nettle, berries, and more.
 
Test your plant-based pigments on watercolour paper, including creating a holiday card. Participants will choose two plaster miniature botanical casts to paint and take home or gift for the holiday season. These ornaments are created by Rebecca, each made using impressions of live botanicals. This workshop features botanical casts made with flowers directly from Toronto Botanical Garden, capturing the garden’s beauty in artwork that lasts long after the blossoms fade.
 
All materials will be provided. No prior experience required.
 
This workshop is intended for ages 16+. Mature youth aged 12+ are welcome, but must be accompanied and supervised by an adult.
 
Please note: Please wear practical clothes and footwear that you don’t mind getting a little messy. As with all handmade processes using real plants: results will vary, pigments may shift in colour over time, and each piece will have perfect imperfections that contribute to its unique character.
 
Saturday, November 28, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $115, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Rebecca Fortin
Rebecca Fortin is a visual artist based in rural Whitby, Ontario, where she creates botanical artwork rooted in the textures, colours, and quiet beauty of the plants around her. After a 20-year career in public health administration, Rebecca pivoted to focus on her art practice, completing the Drawing and Painting program at the Haliburton School of Art + Design in 2022. She now works full-time as an artist, bringing together her background in community health promotion with her passion for connecting people to nature through art.
 
Rebecca’s work has been shown across Ontario and is held in private and corporate collections in Canada and internationally. Her hands-on workshops invite participants to explore botanicals and natural art materials — offering memorable, calming experiences and the opportunity to create beautiful, one-of-a-kind pieces to take home.

description:

“The truth is that we are one body moving through time together.” — Richard Wagamese 
Are you centered? Open to the energy of joy? Open to moving as one? 
We are all connected. Our DNA remembers this connection through clay. In our cells, we hold the memory of all creation. Guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, explore simple physical practices with clay designed to bring you into the moment while deepening and expanding awareness that we are all connected.

                    Suzanne Thomson, Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist
                    
                
                
                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, registered psychotherapist, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy, and trauma-informed approaches she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. Transformation by Fire: Women Overcoming Violence Through Clay, a 10-year retrospective at the Gardiner Museum facilitated by Suzanne, won the 2013 OMA Award of Excellence in Exhibitions. It is a direct reflection of Suzanne’s deep commitment to working collaboratively to address social justice issues through the arts.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle

description:

A
learning circle

location: York Woods
description:

title: Run Your One-Person Business with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
When you're the whole company, the admin never ends: emails, scheduling, proposals, follow-ups. What if you could design a system to handle the busywork?
In this class, you'll learn to design an administrative system for a one-person business with AI as your assistant: intake pipelines, email drafting, client communication, and scheduling. Learn to map work into four piles: what's rules-based, what AI drafts, what needs your judgment, and what should never be automated. You'll build reusable templates and leave with a clearer plan for how AI could help your business.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Artists in the Library: Origami Lotus Flowers
location: Thorncliffe, Program Room
description:
This is a six-part workshop series that creates a space for exploring belonging and not belonging through conversation and hands-on art-making. Guided by reflective questions, participants engage in practices such as origami with washi, drawing, dyeing, and writing, using the lotus as a shared symbol of transformation and resilience across cultures. The workshops foster an inclusive, supportive environment, particularly for those who feel marginalized or disconnected. The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
The workshops are open to youth, ages 13-17, and require no prior artistic experience.

title: Art of Darkness: Edgar Allan Poe's Life & Work
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?
In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.
Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Emily Ogden
Naben Ruthnum
Read more:

title: Vietnam & Cambodia with Angkor Wat! Ancient Kingdoms of Southeast Asia!!
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

As with all our tailor-made Meetup trips, our expert guides will lead us off the beaten path to uncover the authentic charm of each destination, while comfortable accommodations and delicious local cuisine ensure a truly immersive travel experience. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the vibrant cities and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam, finishing with the wonders of Cambodia.

We begin in Hanoi, where history and culture come alive, then sail the emerald waters of Halong Bay. Step back in time among the imperial treasures of Hue, wander the lantern-lit streets of charming Hoi An, and feel the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. We conclude your adventure at the awe-inspiring temples of Siem Reap, home to the legendary Angkor Wat.

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS:

* **Hanoi**; explore Ho Chi Minh sites, Temple of Literature, Old Quarter cyclo ride & water puppet show
* Visit rural **craft villages**: conical hat & incense making, home-hosted lunch, village walk
* **Ha Long Bay cruise**: limestone islands, floating villages, cave visit, Tai Chi & sunset views
* **Hue**: Perfume River boat ride, Thien Mu Pagoda, Khai Dinh’s Tomb & Imperial Citadel
* Scenic **Hai Van Pass train** to Danang; explore Dragon Bridge, Cham Museum, Marble Mountain
* **Hoi An Ancient Town** (UNESCO), visit tailor shops, pottery village & organic farm with cooking class
* **Ho Chi Minh City & Cu Chi Tunnels**; War Remnants Museum, Reunification Palace & Ben Thanh Market
* **Mekong Delta cruise**: coconut workshops, sampan ride, orchards & lunch in riverside village
* **Siem Reap**: dinner with Apsara dance, Angkor temples (Ta Prohm, Bayon, Angkor Wat)
* Cambodian cultural immersion: **monk blessing**, village crafts & cooking, **Tonle Sap Lake sunset cruise**

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary: **[Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, who know AI from very different angles, united for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).
The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for.
No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become.
Featuring:
Jerrold McGrath
, Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime
Joseph Wilson
, Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines
Owais Lightwala
, Assistant Professor, Performance at The Creative School at Toronto Metropolitan University, Director,
Chrysalis

title: Paper Quilling: Holiday Gnome Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled workshop on paper quilling and learn how to make amazing art with paper strips!
In the spirit of the holidays, join us for a creative and relaxing experience surrounded by the beauty of Toronto Botanical Garden! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn the art of paper quilling and create a stunning artwork from paper strips.
 
Perfect for beginners and craft lovers alike, this session will guide you step by step through rolling, shaping, and assembling paper strips into a masterpiece on a 5″x7″ canvas. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, or enjoying some creative “me time,” you’ll leave with a beautiful handmade piece and a new skill to cherish
 
All materials provided. Suitable for adults and children ages 10 and above.
 
Saturday, December 5, 2 to 4 p.m.
Public $50, TBG Members $45 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe.
This talk will be given by Dr. Pratika Dayal from the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto.
No registration is required, but registering will make sure you receive a reminder.

WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Python Essentials 1
location: Brookbanks, Lower Level Auditorium
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

What if you could build an app just by describing it, with no coding experience needed? That's vibe coding.
In this workshop, you'll use an AI coding assistant to build your own small, useful webpage, checklist, or organizer from scratch. You'll learn the build loop: describe what you want, review the plan, build one feature, test it, fix the bugs, and write documentation so you (or anyone) can understand it later.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. title: Birds and Our Christmas Traditions
location: Mount Pleasant, Basement program room
description:
Birds are woven into the fabric of Christmas traditions, serving as powerful symbols of hope, renewal, and warmth during the winter months. Their presence during the holidays, whether through festive ornaments, songs, or sightings at feeders, recalls ancient lore that connects birds with messages of love and positivity. By inviting birds into our lives and honoring them through tradition, we not only support these treasured visitors but also embrace the spirit of Christmas—one of generosity, harmony, and the celebration of nature’s enduring beauty. Jim Mackiewicz is the owner of Wild Birds Unlimited and has been helping customers with backyard bird feeding and connecting to nature for 25 years.

Early one morning, while delivering an order to the local convent, Bill makes a discovery which forces him to confront both his past and the complicit silences of a town controlled by the church. title: Aesthetics Reading Group (Alexandra King, Simon Fraser University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Aesthetics Reading Group is pleased to welcome as guest speaker Alexandra King, associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Simon Fraser University. Currently, she is thinking through what aesthetic normativity looks like: the shape it takes, its parallels and interactions with other varieties of normativity (like the moral and epistemic), and whether it can be said to exist at all. Within aesthetics, she is also interested in an assortment of issues, including subtlety, high and low art, aesthetic/artistic agency, and applied arts. She also owns, runs, and regularly writes for the aesthetics and philosophy of art blog Aesthetics for Birds, which aims to make concepts and arguments in academic aesthetics accessible to a wide, public audience.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Modern Phantoms
description:
As Toronto has grown into a major metropolis, its ghost stories have grown along with it. Many of our city's most bone-chilling tales were born out of that rapid evolution — and the sense of unease it has often caused. We'll conclude this series of talks with author Adam Bunch by exploring ghost stories from Toronto's more recent past. We'll take the subway with the spectre believed to haunt the TTC, set sail with the ghost ship of Etobicoke Creek, and meet the demon said to have terrorized one of Canada's most famous folk singers.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Film Screening: ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
Join us to watch ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See in Inuktitut with English Subtitles.
The film screening will include an 82 minute film and a 20 minute pre-recorded Q&A (102 minutes total).
Blurring the line between narrative and non-fiction, Uyarak and her eldest sister Saqpinak, embark on a difficult healing journey after a traumatic event that reminds them of the importance of community, culture, and family.
Feel free to drop in, no registration required. Registering will send you a reminder before the event.
SYNOPSIS: After experiencing a traumatic event in Igloolik (an Inuit hamlet in Foxe Basin, Qikiqtaaluk Region in Nunavut), Uyarak leaves her community and family in Nunavut to live in Montréal. When Covid-19 lockdowns close off the Canadian Arctic from the rest of the world, Uyarak is further separated from her closest friend, eldest sister, Saqpinak. This extreme situation blurs the lines of both the fictional lives of the sisters, and the non-fiction lives of the film’s directors, Lucy Tulugarjuk and Carol Kunnuk, who play the sisters. The film becomes a series of vignettes of heartache and healing – both in the dramatic based-on-true-events narrative, and the lived reality of these characters and creators. Uyarak doesn’t remember much about one terrible night of domestic violence, but Saqpinak does. Through Zoom calls, Uyarak talks about healing from years of trauma and abuse, and how the counselling sessions she goes to, and other cultural reconnections, are helping her heal. At the same time, Saqpinak is raising a family and hosting live shows about her community. Things are difficult at home – Saqpinak herself is experiencing domestic abuse at home but is waiting to talk about this to Uyarak when she can get home. When Covid-19 restrictions ease, Uyarak is finally able to travel home to Igloolik. At home, she embarks on a deeper healing journey visiting with family and elders, in town, and out on the land. Uyarak and Saqpinak share more stories and support one another in their short time together before Uyarak must return to Montréal.
ABOUT THE CO-DIRECTORS: Lucy Tulugarjuk is an award-winning actor, creative performer, and the Executive Director of Nunavut Independent Television Network (NITV). NITV created Canada’s first 24/7 Inuit language television station, Uvagut TV. Lucy is the co-writer, director of Tia and Piujuq, and assistant director for Zacharias Kunuk’s, One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk. In addition to her work in film and television, Lucy is a skilled Inuktitut translator. Carol Kunnuk is a filmmaker working in independent television and film with Isuma for over 25 years as a writer, camera operator, production supervisor, assistant director, actor, and editor. Her personal work includes the short, Being Prepared (NFB), and creator/director of the documentary, Attagatuluk. Carol currently directs and produces Welcome to my Qammaq, a weekly live television show broadcasting across Canada on Uvagut TV.

title: Nerikomi with Eiko Maeda | Nov 14 & 15 2026 | Dupont
location: 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Join us for a two-day workshop with ceramic artist Eiko Maeda, exploring the traditional Japanese technique of Nerikomi. Unlike surface decoration, Nerikomi builds pattern directly into the clay body itself, layering, stacking, and folding differently coloured clays until intricate designs run through the material from edge to edge. Over two days, you'll learn to prepare and condition coloured clays, build your own pattern blocks and work through four distinct pattern designs, each resulting in a finished ceramic piece approximately 15 cm in diameter. Eiko will guide you through every stage, from initial slab to shaped, refined form. This workshop is open to makers at all levels. No prior experience with Nerikomi is required, though some familiarity with hand-building is an asset. ABOUT EIKO MAEDA Eiko Maeda trained in Japanese lacquer at Joshibi University of Art and Design in Tokyo before discovering ceramics after relocating to Canada. She has spent over a decade developing and teaching her Nerikomi practice from her studio in Ontario, and has been recognized by the Ontario Arts Council and the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair. In 2026, her work was exhibited in Taipei, Taiwan. PLEASE NOTE Firing is included in the registration fee. Finished works will be available for pick-up approximately 3–4 weeks after the workshop concludes. You will be notified by email when your pieces are ready. All Specialty tools will be available for usage with the option to purchase your tools at the end of the course., Toronto, ON
